definitions.name: flexure_arc
definitions.signature: x: float, z: float, x_start: float, length: float, angle_deg: float
definitions.documentation:
Map a point aft of the flexure start through a circular bend.

Circular-flexure arc (reused from morphing-airfoil model.py:warp): the
spine is assumed to bend into an arc of constant curvature that preserves
arc length after x_start. kappa = angle/length (rad/mm). Positive angle is
trailing-edge down. This is an imposed kinematic target, not an elastic
equilibrium shape; skin/rib stiffness and spar reaction are omitted.

definitions.name: _crank_angle
definitions.signature: center, target, r: float, length: float, servo_limit_deg: float=60.0
definitions.documentation:
Solve the rotary-crank four-bar for the crank angle that closes the loop.

The crank pin sweeps a circle of radius `r` about `center` with the
convention pin = center + r*(sin t, cos t), so t = 0 is straight up (+z).
The pushrod runs pin -> `target` and has a FIXED length `length` (set at the
neutral target); the crank rotates until the pin lands at that distance from
`target`. Derivation: |pin - target| = length is a law-of-cosines problem in
the triangle (center, pin, target); with D = target - center, dist = |D| and
k = (dist^2 + r^2 - length^2)/(2 r dist), the two branches are
t = atan2(dz, dx) +- asin(k). The nearest branch wins; overtravel (|k|>1 or
|t|>servo_limit_deg) raises rather than stretching the rod.

definitions.name: linkage
definitions.signature: center, target0, r: float, angle_deg: float, flexure_start: float, flexure_len: float, servo_limit_deg: float=60.0
definitions.documentation:
Solve the servo-crank/pushrod four-bar for one flexure bend angle.

Reused from morphing-airfoil model.py:linkage. `center` is the servo output
axis (x, z); `target0` is the rib-horn pin at neutral; `r` is the crank
radius. The horn moves with the flexure arc; the crank rotates until the
fixed-length pushrod closes the loop. Returns the nearest valid crank
branch and raises ValueError on overtravel (never stretches the rod).

definitions.name: linkage_external
definitions.signature: servo_center, servo_arm_r: float, horn_pivot, horn_r: float, bend_deg: float, servo_limit_deg: float=60.0
definitions.documentation:
External horn + pushrod four-bar (stock-aileron style), for the panel-bay servo.

The zone output horn is a rigid bellcrank pivoting about `horn_pivot` (the
hinge axis); its pin sits `horn_r` below the pivot at neutral and rotates
1:1 with the commanded flexure bend `bend_deg` (positive = trailing edge
down, pin sweeps aft) — the spanwise sync rod carries that rotation to the
flexible ribs, so the bellcrank angle equals the flexure bend angle. The
servo sits in the panel bay with its output axis at `servo_center` and its
arm (`servo_arm_r`) hanging below the centre; a fixed-length pushrod joins
the arm pin to the horn pin through the existing cover exit. Screening
kinematics only — no servo torque, rod bending or friction.

definitions.name: transmission_angle
definitions.signature: pin: tuple, target: tuple, crank_center: tuple
definitions.documentation:
Four-bar transmission angle: between the pushrod and the crank arm.

The pushrod runs pin->target; the crank arm runs crank_center->pin. A
transmission angle near 90 deg gives the best mechanical advantage; the
declared minimum is 30 deg (classic four-bar rule of thumb). Returns
degrees in [0, 90].

definitions.name: flexure_strain
definitions.signature: t_spine: float, flexure_len: float, angle_deg: float
definitions.documentation:
Nominal spine surface strain for a circular bend.

strain = kappa * t/2 with kappa = delta/L_f, so strain = delta_rad * t / (2 L_f).
Reused from morphing-airfoil model.py:calculate (nominal_spine_surface_strain).
This is thickness x curvature / 2; local posts, horn loading and fatigue
concentration invalidate it as a life criterion.

definitions.name: rib_stations
definitions.signature: y0: float, y1: float, pitch: float, inset: float
definitions.documentation:
Spanwise rib stations: end ribs `inset` inside the zone ends, then `pitch`.

Returns ascending y positions. The first and last ribs sit at y0+inset and
y1-inset; interior ribs are spaced by `pitch`. The end ribs are inset so
the sync-rod and spar ends have printed material beyond them.

definitions.name: servo_fit_station
definitions.signature: station: dict, servo_h: float, wall: float
definitions.documentation:
Decide where the servo fits inside the local section.

The servo needs servo_h + 2*wall of local thickness at its chordwise
centre. Scan the measured thickness samples for the aftmost chord station
(closest to the hinge) that fits, and return the offset forward of the
hinge. This is the honest packaging check: the servo is never shrunk.

definitions.name: servo_box_fit
definitions.signature: station: dict, servo: dict, wall: float, fairing_mm: float=0.0, aft_limit: float | None=None
definitions.documentation:
Fit the full servo box (l chordwise x h vertical) forward of the aft limit.

The servo sits in the wing panel's aileron servo bay, entirely forward of
the aft limit (the aileron hinge for the measured path, or the rear-web
plane for the generated path), with its long axis chordwise and its `h`
axis vertical (output shaft down, through the lower-skin / servo-cover
opening). The shaft face sits on the lower skin, so the section must clear
`h + wall` between the lower skin and the upper skin over the whole
chordwise footprint `[x - l/2, x + l/2]`; `fairing_mm` is the extra depth
the servo cover adds below the lower skin. Returns the AFT-most chord
centre that fits, plus a pure-airfoil verdict and the fairing depth
actually required.

definitions.name: mount_loads
definitions.documentation:
Four-foot equilibrium under bounded shaft force, torque and inertia cases.

Foot coordinates are (x,z); normal load is +Y uplift. Positive moments follow
the right-hand rule. The shaft is H above the support plane. Each case includes
simultaneous axial load, radial direction, gravity and a signed inertia axis.
The elastic bolt-group helper supplies in-plane direct + eccentric shear. Normal
forces use a rigid four-point plate distribution, before a declared prying factor.

The sleeve variant transfers shear by positive bore bearing, not by pretending
that sleeve-only preload clamps the plastic. A clearance movement allowance is
therefore retained. The insert variant has only a declared pull-out sensitivity;
its measured pull-out, rotation and creep are still mandatory open gates.

definitions.name: mobility
definitions.documentation:
Return first-order mobility of the declared ideal rigid-body joint graph.

Each body has three translations and three rotations. A revolute joint
equates velocity at its pivot (three rows) and the two transverse angular
velocities (two rows). A positive angular lock adds the axial row. Scaling
translations by a characteristic length avoids a units-driven rank result.
Nonzero infinitesimal mobility does NOT prove a finite folding branch; zero
locked mobility is an ideal kinematic result, not stiffness/preload testing.

definitions.name: radial_gland_check
definitions.signature: cs, bore_d, groove_root_d, groove_w, diam_tol, growth_frac, cs_tolerance, width_tol=0.0, stretch_max=0.0
definitions.documentation:
Squeeze and fill of a static piston gland, nominal and worst case.

squeeze = (cs − radial gap) / cs, where radial gap = (bore − groove root) / 2
fill    = O-ring section area / groove area = (π cs² / 4) / (groove_w × radial gap)
Worst case stacks the ±cs tolerance, a ± process tolerance on both diameters (halved into
the radial gap) and the moisture growth. Both mating parts are the same material, so growth
scales the gap by `growth_frac` rather than opening it.
Optional width tolerance and maximum installed stretch support printed glands.
The minimum cross-section uses incompressible area scaling, cs/sqrt(1+stretch),
as a declared screening approximation; it is not an elastomer/contact solve.
Zero optional allowances preserve historical finished-gland calculations.
Returns a dict of fractions. All tolerances are bilateral absolute mm.

definitions.name: gap_channels
definitions.documentation:
Thin gaps along coil faces, heated on the coil wall only: the topology-neutral winding channel.

Radial machine: n_faces = 2 × slots, flow_len = stack, face_width = radial coil depth.
Axial-flux coil tray: n_faces = 2 × coils, flow_len = radial coil length, face_width = axial coil thickness.
`end_area_m2` adds end-turn surface wetted at the same film coefficient (declared, as in `case.hydraulics`).

definitions.name: evaluate
definitions.documentation: Temperatures, pressure drop and utilisation of one design point. `fraction` = share of flow through the winding (metered only).

definitions.name: _flow_at_budget
definitions.documentation: Largest jacket flow within the pump budget and the flow cap (Δp rises monotonically with flow).

definitions.name: _score
definitions.documentation: The jacket is designed against the stator limits it controls; the rotor is reported, not traded.

definitions.name: _best_fraction
definitions.documentation: Metered split minimising the worse of coil and iron utilisation (unimodal: golden section).

definitions.name: design
definitions.documentation:
Choose gap, flow and (for metered) split for each arrangement; rank by stator loss headroom.

Returns dict(best=…, by_arrangement={…}, as_built=None). Flow is the largest the pump budget and
the flow cap allow: more oil never heats a laminar design, it only costs pump power, which is reported.

definitions.name: flow_at_budget
definitions.documentation: Public name of the pump-budget flow rule (L/min).

definitions.name: report
definitions.documentation: Plain JSON-able summary: the chosen design, every arrangement's optimum and the as-built point.

definitions.name: geopotential
definitions.documentation: Geometric height above MSL -> geopotential height H = r0 z/(r0 + z) (US76 eq. 18).

definitions.name: T_std
definitions.documentation: US76 standard temperature [K] at geopotential height H (clamped to the model top).

definitions.name: column_P
definitions.documentation:
Relative hydrostatic pressure P(H) = p(H)/p(0) of the US76 column with every layer shifted by dT [K]
(H geopotential, clamped to the model top). dT=0 reproduces the US76 pressure ratio.

definitions.name: vapour_e_pa
definitions.signature: H, T, p, Hs, dT_K, p0_pa, rh
definitions.documentation:
Water-vapour partial pressure [Pa]. rh applies up to the tropopause (H_TROPO_M, geopotential); above it the
vapour MOLE FRACTION is held at its tropopause value (cold-trap; stratospheric H2O is ~constant, few ppmv).
v0.2.0 applied rh at all heights: e exceeded p near 51 km (rho < 0, NaN sound speed) and rho was off by
tens of % above ~20 km. Bit-identical to v0.2.0 at H <= H_TROPO_M. MODELED.

definitions.name: ref_state
definitions.signature: z_world, site_elev_m=0.0, dT_K=0.0, p0_pa=P0_PA, rh=0.0, geometric=True, column=None
definitions.documentation:
Air state at heights z_world [m] above the site (world z=0 is the ground at site_elev_m MSL).
geometric=True (v0.2 default): heights are geometric and converted to geopotential (US76);
False: v0.1 convention (height used directly as geopotential; differs by z^2/r0, 0.4 m at 1.6 km).
column: optional measured / forecast column (see column_nodes); None = the ISA + dT column (unchanged).
Returns dict of arrays: T_K, p_pa, rho, c (dry, legacy sensor form), c_moist, e_pa, mu, nu.

definitions.documentation: Column table -> node array [N, 6] (see the block comment above). Cached per (column, atmos).

definitions.name: column_eval
definitions.documentation: (T_K, p_pa, x_w) at geopotential heights H from column nodes (host twin of core/atmos.col_state).

definitions.name: column_state
definitions.documentation: ref_state() for a column (same keys).

definitions.name: surface_to_atmos
definitions.documentation:
Inverse of ref_state at the ground: the atmos dict (site_elev_m, dT_K, p0_pa, rh) whose z=0 state is
exactly temp_c / pressure_pa. Use this instead of hand-mirroring the ISA (e.g. legacy sensor flags -> core).

definitions.name: psi_m
definitions.documentation:
Momentum stability function. Unstable: Paulson 1970 / Dyer 1974. Stable: Businger-Dyer -5 z/L (default,
same as legacy sensor env_atmos; valid only to z/L ~ 1) or, with bh91=True, Beljaars & Holtslag (1991) eq. 28,
which stays physical in strongly stable air (z/L >> 1).

definitions.name: phi_m
definitions.documentation: Dimensionless shear phi_m = 1 - zL dpsi/dzL (consistent with psi_m).

definitions.name: mos_speed
definitions.signature: z, u_star, z0, inv_L, z_cap, bh91=False
definitions.documentation: Surface-layer MOS speed, held at u(z_cap) above z_cap (the v0.1 'cap' profile).

definitions.name: bl_setup
definitions.signature: u10=0.0, wind_dir_deg=270.0, z0=0.05, obukhov_L=float('inf'), z_cap=100.0, profile='bl', lat_deg=40.0, bl_height_m=None, geostrophic_speed=None, geostrophic_dir_deg=None, free_shear_per_km=0.0, free_veer_deg_per_km=0.0, uniform_speed=None, stable_psi='bd', table=None, **_ignored
definitions.documentation:
All derived mean-wind parameters (dict) from the Env wind config. Extra keys (turbulence, seed, ...)
are ignored so an Env 'wind' dict can be passed as **cfg.

definitions.name: wind_table
definitions.documentation:
MEASURED / FORECAST wind profile (REAL 2026-10-16): dict(z_agl_m, speed [m/s], dir_from_deg) -> dict(z, s, b)
(b = turning [rad, + clockwise] from the surface FROM direction, unwrapped with height), nodes above z_s only.
When present it REPLACES the boundary-layer law above z_s: linear from the surface-layer top (u(z_s), turning 0)
to the first node, linear between nodes, held above the last. The surface layer (MOS) and the turbulence are
unchanged. None -> None.

definitions.name: table_wind
definitions.documentation: (speed, turning) from bl_setup()['table'] at z > z_s (host twin of core/wind._table_wind).

definitions.name: mean_wind
definitions.documentation: (speed [m/s], turning [rad, + clockwise from the surface direction]) at height z for bl_setup() dict b.

definitions.name: mean_wind_enu
definitions.documentation: Mean wind vector (E, N) [m/s] at height z (no gusts).

definitions.name: turb_decay
definitions.documentation: Turbulence sigma multiplier: 1 in the surface layer, Hanna (1982) BL decay above, quiet free troposphere.

THE rigid-body step of the unified sim (every 6-DOF body in every domain goes through here).
p, rot, vel, om_b = current state of body i (values, = x[i], q[i], v[i], w[i]); F_world = total world force

definitions.name: darcy_laminar
definitions.documentation: Fully developed laminar pipe flow: f = 64/Re (valid Re < ~2300).

definitions.name: darcy_haaland
definitions.documentation: Haaland explicit fit to Colebrook: 1/√f = −1.8 log10((ε/D/3.7)^1.11 + 6.9/Re); within ~2 % for Re > 4000.

definitions.name: darcy_swamee_jain
definitions.documentation: Swamee–Jain explicit fit: f = 0.25 / log10(ε/D/3.7 + 5.74/Re^0.9)²; stated range 5000 < Re < 1e8, 1e-6 < ε/D < 0.01.

definitions.name: darcy_colebrook
definitions.documentation:
Colebrook–White, iterated: 1/√f = −2 log10(ε/(3.7 D) + 2.51/(Re √f)); fixed point seeded with Haaland.

Raises ValueError when the log argument is non-positive (no turbulent solution at that Re).

definitions.name: darcy_blasius
definitions.documentation: Blasius smooth-pipe turbulent friction factor: f = 0.316 Re^-0.25 (≈ 4000 < Re < 1e5).

definitions.name: nusselt_dittus_boelter
definitions.documentation: Dittus–Boelter turbulent internal flow: Nu = 0.023 Re^0.8 Pr^n, n = 0.4 heating / 0.3 cooling (Re > 1e4, 0.6 < Pr < 160).

definitions.name: f_re_rect_duct_laminar
definitions.documentation:
Shah & London fully developed laminar f·Re (Darcy) for a rectangular duct of aspect alpha = short/long (0 < alpha ≤ 1).

96 for parallel plates (alpha → 0), ≈ 56.9 for a square duct.

definitions.name: nusselt_rect_duct_laminar_h1
definitions.documentation:
Shah & London fully developed laminar Nu_H1 (uniform axial flux, peripherally uniform wall T), all walls heated.

8.235 for parallel plates, ≈ 3.61 for a square duct.

definitions.name: darcy_petukhov
definitions.documentation: Petukhov smooth-tube Darcy friction factor f = (0.790 ln Re − 1.64)⁻² (≈ 3000 < Re < 5e6).

definitions.name: nusselt_gnielinski
definitions.documentation: Gnielinski Nu = (f/8)(Re − 1000)Pr / (1 + 12.7 √(f/8)(Pr^⅔ − 1)) with Darcy f (≈ 3000 < Re < 5e6, 0.5 < Pr < 2000).

Map COM [Fx,Fy,Fz,Mx,My] to [lower X,Y,upper X,Y,thrust] force.

For small shaft tilts: x(z)=x+z*theta_y and y(z)=y-z*theta_x.

definitions.name: simulate
definitions.documentation:
Run a finite-time 5-DOF sampled rigid-rotor feedback experiment.

All ten coils have current/flux/voltage limits and first-order current
tracking. Position noise, a filtered derivative and whole-sample command
delay are explicit. Gravity and fixed external/magnetic loads are trimmed;
imbalance rotates at shaft speed and force/torque pulses remain untrimmed.
Startup from touchdown is deliberately excluded from this local model.

coverage: Test-text reference only; not measured branch/function coverage.

definitions.name: solve_field
definitions.documentation:
Solve Az on the square grid and return B at the winding radius.

Domain: square of half-width R = 1.35 * rotor outer radius. Cells are
labelled air (nu = 1/mu0), copper (same, mu_r 1), magnet (nu = 1/(mu0*mu_r_m),
plus its M source) and iron (nu = 1/(mu0*mu_r_fe)). The magnetization curl
source is computed per magnet cell from the segment's Halbach angle.

`exterior` flips the magnetization rotation sign — the exterior-field
Halbach pattern — and samples the field OUTSIDE the ring at the winding
radius (the rim-drive geometry: magnets on the prop tips, winding in the
duct wall).

definitions.name: dimensional_longitudinal
definitions.documentation:
Convert non-dimensional longitudinal derivatives to dimensional form (SI).

With qbar = 1/2 rho V^2 and U0 = V (level flight), and the incompressible Mach
terms C_Du = C_Lu = C_mu = 0:

    X_u = -(qbar S/(m V)) (C_Du + 2 CD0)        [1/s]
    X_w =  (qbar S/(m V)) (C_L   - C_Dalpha)    [1/s]
    Z_u = -(qbar S/(m V)) (C_Lu  + 2 C_L)       [1/s]
    Z_w = -(qbar S/(m V)) (C_Lalpha + CD0)      [1/s]
    Z_wdot = (qbar S c/(2 m V^2)) C_Lalphadot   [m/m, dimensionless]
    Z_q = -(qbar S c/(2 m V)) C_Lq              [m/s]
    M_w =  (qbar S c/(Iyy V)) C_malpha          [1/(m s)]
    M_wdot = (qbar S c^2/(2 Iyy V^2)) C_malphadot  [1/m]
    M_q =  (qbar S c^2/(2 Iyy V)) C_mq          [1/s]

Returns a dict of dimensional derivatives plus the dimensionless pitch metric.
The derivatives are already normalised by mass/inertia (Nelson's convention),
i.e. Z_w = dw/dt per w, M_w = dq/dt per w, so no further division is applied
when building the state matrix.

definitions.name: longitudinal_matrix
definitions.documentation:
Build the longitudinal state matrix A (4x4) for x = [u, w, q, theta] (SI).

Level flight (theta0 = 0), stability axes, small perturbations:

    u_dot = X_u u + X_w w + 0 q         - g theta
    w_dot = Z_u u + Z_w w + (Z_q + U0) q
    q_dot = (M_u + M_wdot Z_u) u + (M_w + M_wdot Z_w) w
            + (M_q + M_wdot (U0 + Z_q)) q
    theta_dot = q

The q_dot row folds in the downwash-lag (C_malphadot -> M_wdot) correction by
substituting w_dot into the pitching-moment equation. With M_wdot = 0 this
reduces to the plain [M_u, M_w, M_q] row.

definitions.name: dimensional_lateral
definitions.documentation:
Convert non-dimensional lateral-directional derivatives to dimensional (SI).

With reference b (span), V = U0:

    Y_b = (qbar S/m) C_Ybeta                 [m/s^2]
    L_b = (qbar S b/Ixx) C_lbeta             [1/s^2]
    N_b = (qbar S b/Izz) C_nbeta             [1/s^2]
    Y_p = (qbar S b/(2 m V)) C_Yp            [m/s]
    Y_r = (qbar S b/(2 m V)) C_Yr            [m/s]
    L_p = (qbar S b^2/(2 V Ixx)) C_lp        [1/s]
    L_r = (qbar S b^2/(2 V Ixx)) C_lr        [1/s]
    N_p = (qbar S b^2/(2 V Izz)) C_np        [1/s]
    N_r = (qbar S b^2/(2 V Izz)) C_nr        [1/s]

The roll/yaw derivatives are normalised by inertia (Nelson's convention):
L_b = dp/dt per beta, N_b = dr/dt per beta, etc.

definitions.name: lateral_matrix
definitions.documentation:
Build the lateral state matrix A (4x4) for x = [v, p, r, phi] (SI).

Level flight (theta0 = 0), stability axes, small perturbations, and using
beta = v/U0 so that a per-beta derivative acts on v with the factor 1/U0:

    v_dot = (Y_b/U0) v + Y_p p + (Y_r - U0) r + g phi
    p_dot = (L_b/U0) v + L_p p + L_r r
    r_dot = (N_b/U0) v + N_p p + N_r r
    phi_dot = p

Product-of-inertia (Ixz) coupling is applied when mass['Ixz'] is non-zero,
using the standard roll/yaw coupling form (Nelson Eq. 5.62): with
Gamma = 1 - Ixz^2/(Ixx Izz), the coupled inertia rolls/yaw accelerations are
    p_dot = (L + (Ixz/Ixx) N)/Gamma
    r_dot = (N + (Ixz/Izz) L)/Gamma
where L, N are the dimensional rolling/yawing moment accelerations.

definitions.name: eigenmode_metrics
definitions.documentation:
Return mode metrics for a list of eigenvalues (SI, 1/s).

Complex conjugate pair (assume im > 0 branch present): omega_n = |lambda|,
zeta = -Re/|lambda|. Real stable root lambda<0: time constant tau = -1/lambda.
Real unstable root lambda>0: time to double T2 = ln 2 / lambda.

definitions.name: _content
definitions.documentation: Return the normalised magnitude of each component of an eigenvector.

definitions.name: identify_longitudinal_modes
definitions.documentation:
Identify the short-period and phugoid modes of a 4x4 longitudinal A matrix.

Identification uses eigenvector CONTENT, not eigenvalue ordering: the phugoid is
dominated by u and theta (speed/height exchange), the short period by w (=alpha)
and q (pitch). A phugoid score (|u|+|theta|)/(|w|+|q|) is computed for each
oscillatory pair; the higher score is the phugoid. If the short period has
collapsed to real roots, it is reported as such. Returns {mode: {metrics, content}}.

``evals``/``evecs`` may be passed pre-computed (columns of ``evecs`` match
``evals``) so callers can test order-independence directly.

definitions.name: identify_lateral_modes
definitions.documentation:
Identify the Dutch-roll, roll and spiral modes of a 4x4 lateral A matrix.

The Dutch roll is the oscillatory pair (v/beta and r content). The two real roots
are separated by eigenvector CONTENT: the roll mode is p-dominant, the spiral mode
is phi-dominant; ties fall back to |lambda| magnitude (roll is the faster root).

``evals``/``evecs`` may be passed pre-computed (columns match) for order testing.

definitions.name: evaluate_longitudinal
definitions.documentation:
Run the longitudinal model and its handling-quality checks.

Returns the schema result shape {inputs, values, checks, findings, method, declared}.
Checks (declared, linear-theory screens):
  * short period damping ratio within [zeta_min, zeta_max]
  * phugoid damping ratio above zeta_min

definitions.name: evaluate_lateral
definitions.documentation:
Run the lateral-directional model and its handling-quality checks.

Checks (declared, linear-theory screens):
  * Dutch roll damping ratio >= zeta_min AND zeta*omega_n >= zeta_omega_min
  * roll mode time constant <= roll_tau_max_s
  * spiral: stable, or time-to-double >= spiral_t2_min_s

definitions.name: LatticeSurface
definitions.documentation:
Adapter exposing a mean-surface sampler as kernel-style quads.

Mirrors the source LatticeSurface API: ``mesh_thin_surface('quad', chord_panels,
cosine, add_camber)`` returns (points, faces) with faces ordered
[FL, BL, BR, FR] (front = leading edge, back = trailing edge, left/right =
spanwise), the exact convention the vendored kernel's ``solve`` consumes.
``reverse`` flips span ordering so a mirrored half still winds with +z normals.

definitions.name: _interp_stations
definitions.documentation:
Return (y, le_x, chord, z_le, twist) interpolators of span fraction s in [0,1].

Stations are ascending-y dicts with keys y (mm), le_x (mm), chord (mm),
z_chord (mm, leading-edge z of the mean chord line), twist_deg.  All geometry
is converted to metres here; angles to radians.  Linear interpolation in the
normalised span coordinate (root=0, tip=1).

definitions.name: surface_sampler
definitions.documentation:
Return f(s, x) -> (x_m, y_m, z_m) for a mean surface from its stations.

s = span fraction (0 root -> 1 tip), x = chord fraction (0 LE -> 1 TE).
The chord line tilts with the local twist about the leading edge:
z = z_le - chord * x * tan(twist).  ``mirror`` = -1 mirrors y (port half).

definitions.name: camber_slope
definitions.documentation:
Mean camber-line slope dzc/dx of an airfoil section, as a callable of x/c.

``airfoil_coords`` are [x/c, z/c] pairs ordered TE -> upper -> LE -> lower -> TE
(the contract airfoil format).  The camber line is the upper/lower mean at each
x/c, and the slope is its central difference on a uniform chord grid.  For a flat
or symmetric section this returns 0 everywhere (no camber boundary condition).

Thin-airfoil principle: a cambered section behaves like a flat plate rotated by
the camber-line slope, so the boundary condition is n_eff = normalize(n - s t)
with s = dzc/dx and t the chord axis.  Units: dimensionless (d(z/c)/d(x/c)).
Assumes the coords are normalised and closed at the TE; omits thickness (the VLM
mean surface is the camber line, not the skin).

definitions.name: camber_from_config
definitions.documentation:
Return {surface_name: slope-callable} for the airfoil camber in ``config``.

The wing airfoil comes from ``config['airfoil']['coords']`` (selected by
configure.py).  The V-tail has no measured airfoil and is left flat (declared
small effect on CL0/Cm0/trim).  Returns {} when no airfoil is supplied, so all
synthetic/flat tests keep the flat-plate behaviour.

definitions.name: Lattice
definitions.documentation:
Concatenated vortex-lattice geometry with per-panel metadata.

Attributes (all SI metres / radians):
  quads   (N,4,3) FL,BL,BR,FR vertices
  left,right (N,3) bound-vortex endpoints (quarter-chord, panel span edges)
  centre  (N,3) bound-vortex midpoints
  colloc  (N,3) collocation points (3/4 chord, mid-span)
  normals (N,3) unit geometric normals
  chord_axis (N,3) unit chord direction (LE->TE)
  span_axis (N,3) unit bound-vortex direction
  area    (N,)  panel area
  x_frac  (N,)  chord fraction of the panel centre
  y_abs   (N,)  absolute spanwise coordinate of the panel centre
  surface (N,)  int 0=wing, 1=tail
  half    (N,)  int +1 right, -1 left
  strip   (N,)  spanwise strip index (for grouped load distribution)

definitions.name: _append_surface
definitions.signature: lat, quads, strip0, surface_id, half, chordwise
definitions.documentation:
Append one surface's quads to the lattice and compute its panel metadata.

Quads are ordered spanwise-outer / chordwise-inner (i*chordwise + j), so the
spanwise strip index of panel p is p // chordwise.

definitions.name: build_lattice
definitions.documentation:
Build the full aircraft lattice (wing both halves + V-tail both halves).

Cosine spacing in span (per the source adapter) and in chord (per the kernel).
The right half is built root->tip; the left half is the mirror with reversed
span ordering so its panels keep +z normals and +y bound vortices.

definitions.name: effective_normals
definitions.documentation:
Per-panel boundary-condition normals after camber and control deflections.

``camber`` is an optional dict ``{surface_name: slope_fn}`` (see
:func:`camber_from_config`); for each panel of that surface the geometric normal
is rotated in the (chord, normal) plane by the section's mean camber-line slope
s = dzc/dx, i.e. ``n_eff = normalise(n - s * chord_axis)``.

``deflections`` is a list of dicts::

    {"surface": "wing"|"tail", "half": +1|-1|0 (0 = both),
     "mode": "morph"|"flap",
     "x_start": float (chord fraction where the deflection begins),
     "delta_deg": float (positive = trailing edge DOWN),
     "y0", "y1": optional absolute-y span limits (metres) restricting the zone}

For a panel with chord fraction x beyond x_start, the local slope increment is
  s = -tan(delta) * ramp,   ramp = 1 (flap) or (x - x_start)/(1 - x_start)
(morph).  The normal is rotated in the (chord, normal) plane:
  n_eff = normalise(n - s * chord_axis),
i.e. about the local span axis, so the mesh geometry is never moved.  Camber is
applied first, then deflections; both are small rotations about the span axis and
compose additively to first order.

definitions.name: solve_lattice
definitions.signature: lat, velocity, density, reference, normals=None, core_m=1e-07, chunk=128
definitions.documentation:
Solve the linear vortex-lattice system with the vendored Biot-Savart core.

``velocity`` is the freestream at each panel, either a constant (3,) or a
per-panel (N,3) array (used for body-rate boundary conditions).  ``normals``
overrides the geometric panel normals (morph/flap boundary condition).  Returns
dict with F_g (3,), M_g (3,) about ``reference``, gamma (N,), panel_forces (N,3),
centres (N,3), and the boundary residual.

Formula (Kutta-Joukowski at each bound vortex): F_i = rho * V_i x (gamma_i * span),
M_i = (centre_i - reference) x F_i.  The influence matrix is A_ij = n_i . v_ij
with v_ij the unit-circulation induced velocity of horseshoe j at collocation i;
the boundary condition is A gamma = -n . V_inf.

definitions.name: VLMSystem
definitions.documentation:
Cached linear system for many solves on one lattice + deflection state.

The influence matrix (and its LU factorisation) depends only on the lattice
geometry and the effective panel normals (i.e. the deflection state), not on the
freestream.  Building it once and reusing the factors for many right-hand sides
(angles of attack, sideslips, body rates) makes the derivative sweeps cheap.

definitions.name: wake_velocity
definitions.documentation:
Unit-circulation velocity at M points from the two semi-infinite trailing
filaments of N horseshoes (the wake-only part of the kernel's ``horseshoe``).

Reproduces the kernel's wake terms exactly: for filaments starting at ``left``
and ``right`` extending along ``direction``, the induced velocity is
(-d x a * wa + d x b * wb) / (4 pi), with wa = (1 + a.d/|a|)/(|d x a|^2 + core^2).
Reference implementation kept for the kernel's wake decomposition; induced drag
is computed by the lifting-line ``trefftz_induced_drag``.  Not a viscous wake.

definitions.name: strip_circulation
definitions.documentation:
Total bound circulation per spanwise strip, sorted by ascending span y.

``surface_id`` restricts to one surface (0=wing, 1=tail); None uses all panels.
Returns (y_c, Gamma_c, dy_c): strip centres, strip circulations (sum of the
chordwise panel circulations) and strip spanwise widths.

definitions.name: trefftz_induced_drag
definitions.documentation:
Induced drag from the Trefftz-plane trailing vortex sheet (lifting-line form).

Uses the WING panels only: the wing is planar (z=0) so the lifting-line sheet
discretisation applies; the V-tail's own induced drag is omitted (declared small
— the tail is a lightly loaded, low-aspect surface and its induced drag is a
second-order term on total drag).  Each wing strip's total circulation Gamma(y)
forms a trailing vortex sheet whose shed vorticity at each strip edge is the drop
in circulation.  The downwash at each strip centre is the sum of the edge-vortex
contributions (evaluating at strip centres avoids the self-singularity):
  w_k = sum_j shed_j / (4 pi (y_k - y_edge_j)),
  D_i = rho sum_k Gamma_k w_k dy_k.
For elliptic loading this recovers CDi = CL^2/(pi AR) (span efficiency ~1).
Approximate: lifting-line discretisation, not the exact far Trefftz plane.

definitions.name: coefficients
definitions.signature: lat, F_g, M_g, rho, V, reference, D_i=None
definitions.documentation: Convert solver force/moment (solver frame) into stability-axis coefficients.

definitions.name: spanwise_load
definitions.documentation:
Spanwise lift distribution: per-spanwise-strip circulation and lift.

``surface_id`` restricts to one surface (0=wing, 1=tail); None uses all panels.
Strips are the spanwise panel indices; circulation is summed over the chordwise
panels of each strip, and the strip lift is the Kutta-Joukowski form
rho V gamma_strip dy.  ``lift_per_span`` is rho V gamma_strip (N/m, the lift per
unit span that structure tasks consume); ``loading`` is the dimensionless span
loading 2 gamma_strip / (V * mac).  Returns dicts of arrays plus a combined list.

definitions.name: solve
definitions.signature: config, alpha_deg=0.0, beta_deg=0.0, rates=None, deflections=None, reference=None, rho=None, V_ms=None, spanwise=24, chordwise=6, core_m=1e-07
definitions.documentation:
Solve one flight condition and return the full result dict.

``rates`` = (p, q, r) in the standard body convention (rad/s, about the
standard x-forward/z-down axes) — internally mapped to the solver frame.
``reference`` defaults to the CG x from ``config['flight']`` at y=z=0.

definitions.name: freestream_velocity
definitions.signature: V, alpha_deg, beta_deg, rates=None, positions=None, rotation_center=None
definitions.documentation:
Freestream velocity (3,) or (N,3) in the solver frame, including body rates.

V_inf = V (cos a cos b, -sin b, sin a cos b).  Body rates ``(p, q, r)`` are the
standard convention (about x-forward/y-right/z-down); mapped to the solver frame
the angular velocity is omega = (-p, q, -r) about the rotation centre.

definitions.name: convergence
definitions.documentation:
Convergence helper: solve at base and refined panel counts, report the change.

Returns the CL_alpha computed at each level and the relative change between the
base and refined meshes.

coverage: Test-text reference only; not measured branch/function coverage.

definitions.name: properties
definitions.documentation:
Return dry-air or fresh-water properties; water must be single-phase liquid.

Air uses the ideal-gas law and Sutherland viscosity. Water uses IAPWS-IF97
with IAPWS transport properties through pinned iapws 1.5.4. The water
property package accepts MPa, hence the explicit Pa/1e6 conversion.

definitions.name: point_distance
definitions.documentation: Measure Euclidean, axial and lateral separation of two assembled XYZ points.

definitions.name: gap_from_points
definitions.documentation:
Translate upstream FAN along +Z to reach a point-to-point distance.

A belongs to FAN and B to stationary STATOR, both in assembled coordinates.
Lateral offsets stay fixed. A must start upstream (higher Z). Distance is
therefore not interchangeable with axial clearance when radii differ.

definitions.name: similarity_screen
definitions.documentation:
Return an ideal load screen, explicitly without a gap-performance model.

Constant flow and loading coefficients imply Q~n, T~rho*n² and P~rho*n³.
Viscous effects, separation and cavitation can violate these assumptions,
so this is a scale/load comparison, never a spacing ranking or CFD result.
The old 0.65 'projected thrust' multiplier is deliberately not propagated.

coverage: Test-text reference only; not measured branch/function coverage.

definitions.name: _cg_reference
definitions.documentation: Reference point (metres) at the CG: x = flight.cg_x, y=z=0.

definitions.name: _coef
definitions.signature: config, sys_, ref, alpha=0.0, beta=0.0, rates=None
definitions.documentation: Coefficients for one velocity field on a pre-built VLMSystem.

definitions.name: _limit
definitions.documentation: Acceptance limit `key` from config['limits'] (parametric override, integrator addition 2026-09-15 02:15 MDT | 2026-09-15 04:15 EDT | 2026-09-15 08:15 Zulu), else config['declared'].

definitions.name: morph_deflections
definitions.documentation:
Deflection list for the wing morph zones.

``delta_deg`` > 0 = trailing edge DOWN (more camber, more lift).  If
``differential``, the right half deflects -delta (TE up) and the left +delta
(TE down) — the conventional aileron sense producing a right roll for delta>0.

definitions.name: flap_deflections
definitions.documentation:
Deflection list for the conventional hinged ailerons (plain flap) for
comparison against the morph zones; same differential sense as morph.

Uses the measured aileron hinge (``chord_frac`` from the baseline control
surfaces) when present, else the declared 0.65.  The flap spans the union of the
aileron y-ranges, matching the morph-zone span.

definitions.name: ruddervator_deflections
definitions.documentation: Deflection list for the V-tail ruddervators (plain flap on the tail).

definitions.name: _central
definitions.documentation: Central-difference slope of scalar-returning f at 0 with step h.

definitions.name: longitudinal
definitions.documentation:
CL_alpha, Cm_alpha, CL_q, Cm_q about the CG, plus the neutral point and SM.

NP: x_np = x_ref - (dCm/dalpha)/(dCL/dalpha) * c, central differences +/-1 deg.
``body_cm_alpha`` is the declared Munk body pitch-stiffness term (per rad, from
:func:`body_corrections`); it is folded into the body-inclusive NP/SM so the
reported static margin is physical.  Both the VLM-only and body-inclusive NP/SM
are returned (destabilising: the body term moves the NP forward).

definitions.name: lateral_directional
definitions.documentation:
Lateral-directional derivatives Cy_beta, Cn_beta, Cl_beta, Cn_r, Cl_r, Cn_p,
Cl_p from VLM sideslip and body-rate solves, about the CG.

``body_cn_beta`` is the declared Munk body yaw-destabilising term (per rad, from
:func:`body_corrections`); it is folded into the body-inclusive Cn_beta so the
reported directional stability is physical.  Both VLM-only and body-inclusive
values are returned (destabilising: the body term reduces Cn_beta).

definitions.name: vtail_volumes
definitions.documentation:
Horizontal and vertical projected V-tail volume coefficients.

Projection convention: S_h = S_tail cos^2(Gamma), S_v = S_tail sin^2(Gamma)
(Raymer's V-tail projection; the squared factors apportion the dihedral tail
area to its horizontal/vertical roles).  l_t is the tail arm (tail quarter-MAC
x - wing quarter-MAC x).  V_h = S_h l_t /(S c), V_v = S_v l_t /(S b).

definitions.name: control_derivatives
definitions.documentation:
Roll/yaw control from the morph zones, and pitch control from the ruddervator.

Differential morph: Cl_delta_morph, Cn_delta_morph (per rad), and the ratio of
morph vs the original plain aileron (Cl only).  Symmetric ruddervator (elevator):
CL_de and Cm_de (per rad).  Central differences +/-1 deg (six VLM systems total).

definitions.name: roll_authority
definitions.documentation:
Steady non-dimensional roll rate p_hat = p b/(2V) at full morph deflection.

p_hat = - (Cl_delta * delta) / Cl_p  (rolling moment balanced by roll damping).
Accepts precomputed control/lateral derivatives to avoid re-solving.  Also reports
the conventional-aileron p_hat at the same deflection for comparison, and, when
morph p_hat falls below the MIL-F-8785C-style 0.07 target, the deflection that
would reach it (linear in delta) rather than inventing a new limit.

definitions.name: trim
definitions.signature: config, mode='ruddervator', n_load=None, V=None, limit=None, reference=None, spanwise=24, chordwise=6
definitions.documentation:
Trim the symmetric control deflection for Cm = 0 at CL = n W/(q S).

Nested bisection: for each deflection delta, solve alpha so CL(alpha,delta) equals
the required CL, then bisect delta to zero the pitching moment Cm about the CG.
``V`` is the airspeed for the case (default cruise V_ms; the n=4 pull-up uses
V_A).  ``limit`` defaults to the morph +/-12 deg for ``mode="morph"`` and the
declared ruddervator +/-20 deg for ``mode="ruddervator"``.  Reports the trimmed
deflection and angle of attack and whether the deflection is inside limits.

definitions.name: body_corrections
definitions.documentation:
Declared Munk/Gilruth-White slender-body pitch/yaw destabilising corrections.

Cm_alpha,body = +2 * Vol_body / (S * c) per rad (pitch, destabilising: nose-up with
increasing alpha).  Cn_beta,body = -2 * Vol_body / (S * b) per rad (yaw,
destabilising: reduces weathercock stability, DATCOM-style).  The fuselage volume
is a prismatic-of-revolution estimate from the fuselage stations when present,
else 0 (reported as omitted).  These are separate declared corrections folded into
the NP/SM/Cn_beta outputs (not into the raw VLM coefficients).

definitions.name: maneuver_speed
definitions.documentation:
Stall and manoeuvre (corner) speeds from the declared CL_max.

V_stall = sqrt(2 W / (rho S CL_max)); V_A = V_stall * sqrt(n).  ``n`` defaults to
the declared load factor.  CL_max is the declared E205 section value (cited-typical).

definitions.name: _n4_spanwise_load
definitions.documentation:
Wing spanwise lift per unit span (N/m) at the trimmed n=4 pull-up (V_A).

Uses the already-computed n=4 ruddervator trim ``tr``; extracts the wing-only
strip loads (Kutta-Joukowski rho V gamma).  Returns {"y_m": [...],
"lift_N_per_m": [...]} plus the trimmed state, or an empty load when the trim is
not achievable.

definitions.name: _fmt
definitions.documentation: Format a possibly-None value for a finding string.

definitions.name: analyze
definitions.documentation:
Run the full stability analysis and return a schema-shaped result dict.

Adds the round-2 outputs Task C consumes: ``values.derivatives`` (flat, per-rad),
``values.spanwise_load`` (wing lift per span at the trimmed n=4 pull-up), and
``values.reference`` (S, c, b, V_ms, rho, cg_x_mm).  Body pitch/yaw corrections are
folded into NP/SM/Cn_beta (with/without reported); trims are 1 g cruise (V_ms) and
n=4 pull-up (V_A) with a +/-20 deg ruddervator, plus the wing-morph trim at n=4.

coverage: Test-text reference only; not measured branch/function coverage.

definitions.name: normalize
definitions.documentation: Validate physical inputs and bounded volume data; never accept file paths.

definitions.name: write_mesh
definitions.documentation:
Build positive-volume hexahedra in metres with Euler-wall/farfield markers.

Eight geometrically graded layers per face have widths 2dx..256dx.
Only vertices used by fluid cells are written; sealed solid interiors have
no zero-volume/isolated nodes. The browser cell map is saved for review.

definitions.name: configuration
definitions.documentation:
Set physical compressible flow with a stationary, already-rotated body.

AOA/SIDESLIP are zero in SU2 because pose is embedded in the supplied mask.
The original requested angles remain in CASE.json. Euler cannot establish
viscous drag, high-incidence separated flow or thermal material suitability.

definitions.name: read_vtk
definitions.documentation:
Read SU2 ASCII legacy VTK or XML VTU, validating every field count.

SU2 8.5 PARAVIEW_ASCII writes legacy .vtk despite the XML format supported
by its binary writer. Explicit headers avoid interpreting connectivity as data.

definitions.name: parse_volume
definitions.documentation: Average actual SU2 nodal primitives onto the browser's cubic display grid.

definitions.name: runtime_provenance
definitions.documentation:
Hash the executable and immutable inputs immediately before solver launch.

The record identifies this exact local build and mesh/configuration; solver
version strings alone cannot distinguish compiler or configuration changes.

definitions.name: run_job
definitions.documentation: Capture one isolated SU2 run and its true convergence state, even on failure.

definitions.name: start
definitions.documentation: Serialize heavy CFD jobs and retain each run under a unique identifier.

definitions.name: history_trace
definitions.documentation: Read a bounded residual trace, tolerating an incomplete actively written row.

definitions.name: status
definitions.documentation: Return status and a bounded log tail, keeping process objects private.

definitions.name: cancel
definitions.documentation: Terminate only the selected process that this runner started.

definitions.name: saved_cases
definitions.documentation: Index only complete local results with their observed convergence status.

imports: from ..execution import operation as _simulation_operation, report_failure as _simulation_failure
import base64, csv, hashlib, json, math, os, re, signal, subprocess, threading, time
coverage: Packaged implementation; no direct test reference found.

definitions.name: horseshoe
definitions.documentation:
Unit-circulation velocity at M fields from N horseshoes; output M×N×3.

Bound circulation runs left→right. The left wake points inward from
infinity; the right wake points outward. A finite-segment Biot–Savart
kernel uses cross² + core²*segment_length² (both m⁴). Wake denominators
use perpendicular_distance² + core² (both m²). Collinear self terms
vanish through their vector numerators without division by zero.

definitions.name: solve
definitions.signature: surfaces, velocity, density, reference, chord_panels=4, core_m=1e-07, scale=1.0, diagnostics=False
definitions.documentation:
Solve attached, incompressible flow on explicit mean-surface panels.

Surface adapters supply metre-space quads FL,BL,BR,FR. Velocity is a
geometry-axis vector (m/s), density kg/m³ and reference a metre-space point.
Scale changes every geometric length, including the core, for invariance
tests. Results then have the correspondingly scaled force/moment units.
Chunk field evaluations to limit temporary pair-array memory usage.

coverage: Test-text reference only; not measured branch/function coverage.
Packaged implementation; no direct test reference found.

definitions.name: _spacing
definitions.documentation: Cosine (or uniform) x/c grid, n_per_side + 1 points from 0 (LE) to 1 (TE).

definitions.name: _parse_naca
definitions.documentation: Four NACA digits -> (max camber m, camber position p, max thickness t), all fractions.

definitions.name: _naca4_mean_line
definitions.documentation: PDAS four-digit mean line: (yc, dyc/dx) at x/c. Symmetric (m=0) -> (0, 0).

definitions.name: _naca4_half_thickness
definitions.documentation: PDAS half-thickness (fraction) plus the smooth printable-TE term te_thickness_frac/2 * x^4.

definitions.name: _naca_surfaces
definitions.documentation: Upper/lower (x/c, z/c) pairs on grid ``xs`` for a NACA four-digit section.

definitions.name: _lininterp
definitions.documentation: Piecewise-linear interpolation on x-sorted (x, z) rows; clamped at the ends (no overshoot).

definitions.name: _read_numeric
definitions.documentation: Parse float (x, z) rows from a text .dat, skipping comments, blank and non-numeric lines.

definitions.name: _split_surfaces
definitions.documentation:
Split raw .dat rows into x-sorted (upper, lower) surfaces, Selig or Lednicer.

Lednicer: first row holds the two point counts, then upper (LE->TE) and lower (LE->TE)
blocks. Selig: one closed loop TE -> upper -> LE -> lower -> TE, split at the minimum-x
(leading-edge) point. Both returns are ascending in x.

definitions.name: _dat_surfaces
definitions.documentation:
Resample tabulated surfaces on ``xs`` and apply the TE-gap taper (fraction form).

parametric airfoil keeps the measured mean line and tapers the original trailing-edge gap to the
printable thickness: upper += (te_thickness_frac/2 - gap/2) x^4, lower -= (same).

definitions.name: properties
definitions.documentation:
Section properties from a ``coords`` loop: max thickness, max camber and their x/c, and area.

The loop is split at the leading edge (minimum x/c) into x-ascending upper and lower
surfaces; thickness(x) = z_upper(x) - z_lower(x) and camber(x) = (z_upper + z_lower)/2 are
evaluated at the union of both surfaces' x/c breakpoints (exact for the piecewise-linear
surfaces), and area is the shoelace of the closed loop. Returns
``{t_c, t_x, camber_max, camber_x, area}`` — ``t_c``/``camber_max`` in chord fractions,
``area`` in chord^2. ``camber_max`` is the signed maximum mean-line height.

definitions.name: coords
definitions.documentation: NACA four-digit or DAT:<caller-path>; unit chord, closed trailing-edge convention.

coverage: Test-text reference only; not measured branch/function coverage.

definitions.name: outer_and_holes
definitions.documentation:
Slice at coord[axis]==value; return (outer_loop, holes).

``outer_loop`` is the closed loop with the largest enclosed area (the wing
section); ``holes`` are the remaining closed loops (spar tubes and slots).
Both are (N, 2) arrays in the two non-axis source coordinates (Y_src, Z_src
for axis=0). Open chains are ignored (they only occur at joint faces, which
the station lists avoid).

definitions.name: le_te
definitions.documentation:
Return ((z_le, y_le), (z_te, y_te)) for a wing-section polygon in (Y_src, Z_src).

LE is the most-forward point (min Z_src), TE the most-aft (max Z_src). The
chord line height uses the Y_src of those two points.

definitions.name: section_stats
definitions.documentation: Basic station metrics from a wing-section polygon (Y_src, Z_src).

definitions.name: normalize_airfoil
definitions.documentation:
Normalise a wing-section polygon to (x/c, z/c) ordered TE->upper->LE->lower->TE.

Principle: x/c = (Z_src - Z_le)/chord, z/c = (Y_src - z_chord)/chord where
z_chord is the mean Y_src of LE and TE. The upper and lower surfaces are
re-interpolated onto a half-cosine x/c grid (clustered at LE and TE) so the
section has ~2*n_points+2 points. Returns (coords, t_c, camber_max).

definitions.name: fit_circle
definitions.documentation:
Least-squares circle fit (algebraic, Kasa) of a 2D point loop.

Solves x^2+y^2 = D x + E y + F for (D,E,F); centre (D/2, E/2),
r = sqrt(F + cx^2 + cy^2). Returns (cx, cy, r, rms) where rms is the RMS
residual |dist - r|.

definitions.name: classify_hole
definitions.documentation:
Classify a closed hole loop as round (spar tube) or rect (slot).

``poly`` is in (Y_src, Z_src). A hole is round when the least-squares circle
residual is < 8% of its radius; otherwise it is a rectangle (reported by its
chordwise w = Z_src extent and thickness h = Y_src extent). Returns a dict
with shape, size and centre: cy = Y_src centre, cz = Z_src centre.

definitions.name: combine_mass
definitions.documentation:
Combine parts/point-masses into total mass, CG and inertia about the CG.

``items`` is a list of dicts each with mass_g, cg (3,), and either I (3x3
about its own CG) or None (point mass). Returns
(total_g, cg(3,), inertia(3x3) g*mm^2 about the CG). Parallel-axis theorem:
I_CG += I_self + m (|d|^2 I - d d^T), d = cg - CG.

coverage: Test-text reference only; not measured branch/function coverage.

definitions.name: chord_and_le
definitions.signature: family, eta, root_chord, tip_chord, sweep_le_deg, half_span
definitions.documentation: Return chord and leading-edge offset in caller units. Linear, rectangular or truncated elliptical chord; additional leading-edge shear = eta*half_span*tan(sweep).

definitions.name: _spacing_values
definitions.documentation: Spanwise fractions 0..1 for ``n`` stations (``cosine`` or ``uniform``).

definitions.name: stations
definitions.signature: family, half_span, root_chord, tip_chord, sweep_le_deg, dihedral_deg, twist_root_deg, twist_tip_deg, root_le_x, root_z, n, spacing, airfoil=None
definitions.documentation:
Contract §2 wing-station dicts for one half-wing, root (y=0) to tip (y=half_span).

Each station::

  {y, le_x, te_x, chord, z_chord, twist_deg, t_c=None, airfoil, source="generated:<family>"}

with (mm, degrees):

  y        = half_span * f                          (f from ``spacing``)
  chord    = chord_and_le(...)[0]
  le_x     = root_le_x + chord_and_le(...)[1]       (root LE placed at root_le_x)
  te_x     = le_x + chord
  z_chord  = root_z + y * tan(dihedral_deg)         (chord-line height; straight dihedral)
  twist_deg= twist_root_deg + (twist_tip_deg - twist_root_deg) * f   (linear washout)

``spacing`` is "cosine" (stations cluster at root and tip) or "uniform"; elliptical
planforms need cosine for the tip. ``t_c`` is None (the section library fills it), and
``airfoil`` is the caller's profile key (default None). Omissions: dihedral is a
straight tilt that does not change the projected planform area, and y is the flat
projected span coordinate (matching measure.py's planform integral).

definitions.name: area_mac
definitions.documentation:
(area both sides, MAC, MAC LE x, MAC y) by trapezoid integration over the half-span.

With c(y), le_x(y) sampled at ascending stations and both sides doubled (parametric geometry library
README "mean aerodynamic chord is ∫c² ds / ∫c ds"):

  area     = 2 * ∫ c dy                  (mm^2)
  MAC      = ∫ c² dy / ∫ c dy            (mm)
  mac_le_x = ∫ c·le_x dy / ∫ c dy        (mm; chord-weighted average leading edge)
  mac_y    = ∫ c·y dy / ∫ c dy           (mm; chord-weighted spanwise centroid)

Units: mm. Screening: trapezoid rule is exact for a linear taper's area but approximate
for c² (O(h²)); use enough stations. ``le_x`` is read as the absolute LE x at each
station (not the root-relative offset), matching the generated record.

coverage: Test-text reference only; not measured branch/function coverage.

definitions.name: read_stl
definitions.documentation:
Read an STL file, auto-detecting binary vs ASCII.

Binary STL layout (per the CAD authoring format): an 80-byte header, a
uint32 triangle count, then count records of 12 float32 (normal + 3 vertices)
plus a uint16 attribute byte count = 50 bytes per triangle.

Returns ``(vertices, faces)`` where ``vertices`` is an ``(N, 3)`` float64
array of unique vertex coordinates and ``faces`` is an ``(M, 3)`` int64
array of vertex indices (0-based).

definitions.name: read_stl_binary
definitions.documentation: Read a binary STL into a deduplicated ``(vertices, faces)`` pair.

definitions.name: read_stl_ascii
definitions.documentation: Read an ASCII STL (``solid``/``facet normal``/``outer loop``/``vertex``).

definitions.name: mesh_volume
definitions.documentation:
Signed volume of a closed triangle mesh.

Formula (divergence theorem): for a closed surface with outward normals,
    V = (1/6) * sum_over_faces det(v0, v1, v2)
where each face contributes the signed volume of the tetrahedron formed by
that face and the origin. Units are cubic mm for mm inputs.

The sign is + for outward-oriented meshes; use ``abs`` for a physical volume.

definitions.name: mesh_centroid
definitions.documentation:
Centroid of a closed mesh (volume-weighted average of tetra centroids).

The centroid of the tetrahedron ``(0, v0, v1, v2)`` is ``(v0+v1+v2)/4``;
summing each tetrahedron's signed volume times its centroid and normalising
by the total signed volume gives the solid's centroid. Units of mm.

definitions.name: mesh_inertia
definitions.documentation:
Inertia tensor (3x3) of a closed mesh about its centroid, unit density.

Principle: decompose the solid into tetrahedra ``(0, v0, v1, v2)``, one per
face. For a tetrahedron with vertices ``{p0..p3}`` (here ``p0 = 0``),
    J = integral of (x (x^T)) dV = (V/20) * [ sum_k p_k p_k^T + S S^T ],
    S = sum_k p_k,
which follows from integrating barycentric monomials over the simplex
(integral lambda_i lambda_j = (1/120) for i!=j, (1/60) for i==j, with the
simplex-volume factor). Each face contributes its *signed* J.

The inertia tensor about the origin is then ``I0 = tr(J) * I - J``, and the
parallel-axis theorem gives the tensor about the centroid
    ``Ic = I0 - V * (|c|^2 I - c c^T)``.
Units: mm^5 (a mass density of 1 g/mm^3 is implied; multiply by density
for kg·mm²). The returned value is ``(I, volume, centroid)``.

definitions.name: slice_plane
definitions.documentation:
Slice a mesh with a plane ``coord[axis] == value`` into polylines.

Returns ``(closed_loops, open_chains)``, each a list of ``(N, 2)`` float64
arrays in the *two remaining* source coordinates, in source order. For the
DroneENG frame (axes: 0 = X_src span, 1 = Y_src thickness, 2 = Z_src chord),
slicing ``axis=0`` yields (Y_src, Z_src) points.

Method: intersect every triangle with the plane (linear edge interpolation),
collect segments, then stitch endpoints within ``stitch_tol`` (default
0.01 mm — about an order of magnitude above float32 rounding at metre scale)
into closed loops and open chains. Coplanar faces (all three vertices on the
plane) are skipped: their boundary edges are contributed by neighbouring
triangles, avoiding duplicate segments.

definitions.name: _stitch
definitions.documentation:
Stitch loose segments into closed loops and open chains.

Endpoints closer than ``tol`` are merged (coordinates averaged). Walks the
resulting graph, treating degree-2 vertices as polyline interiors; vertices
of degree != 2 terminate a chain. Greedy: for clean slices every vertex has
degree 2 and loops are recovered exactly.

definitions.name: polygon_area
definitions.documentation:
Signed area of a closed polygon by the shoelace formula.

    A = (1/2) * sum_i (x_i y_{i+1} - x_{i+1} y_i)

Positive for counter-clockwise ordering (in a right-handed 2D frame).
Units are mm² for mm inputs.

definitions.name: polyline_length
definitions.documentation: Total length of a polyline (sum of segment norms), mm.

definitions.name: ply_window
definitions.documentation: Projected-slope window (lo, hi) transmitted by one ply (see module docstring). Raises when the slats close the gap.

definitions.name: line_of_sight
definitions.documentation: True when some straight ray passes every ply. Plies are dicts (dir_deg, pitch_mm, slat_mm, depth_mm, tilt_deg).

definitions.name: _duct
definitions.documentation: (Nu, Darcy f) for a rectangular duct of aspect a ≤ 1 at Reynolds re: Shah–London laminar, Gnielinski turbulent, blended.

definitions.name: ply_flow

definitions.documentation: Flow state in one ply of n helical channels (width s, height h) carrying mdot: velocity, Re, Nu, h, Δp.

definitions.name: segment_distance
definitions.documentation: Closest distance between bounded 3-D line segments, including parallel cases.

definitions.name: _positive
definitions.documentation: Never infer material/process numbers from a resin family or source dimensions.

definitions.name: thermal
definitions.documentation:
Steady plug-flow heat exchange, wall power/warmup, and cold-gate conduction screen.

Equal simultaneous unit flow requires balancing/meters; it is an imposed
scenario. Heat transfer is prescribed, not predicted from guessed polymer
properties. Constant-property laminar pressure uses shared ENGToolkit Darcy
correlations. No total injection-pressure or cycle-time rating is returned.

definitions.name: slab_threshold_time
definitions.signature: initial, wall, threshold, half_thickness_m, alpha_m2_s, core_fraction
definitions.documentation:
Time for T(x=fraction*half-thickness) to reach threshold in a fixed-wall slab.

Zero means already below threshold; None means no finite cooling crossing.
A dimensionless series/bisection avoids unstable time stepping and scales as
thickness squared / diffusivity. It excludes latent heat and moving melt.

definitions.name: life_and_timing
definitions.documentation:
Plot measured wear trends against cycles/hours without inventing mold fatigue life.

Calibration is tied to the complete material/process/tooling/route identity.
A new part or thermal recipe invalidates it until applicability is reviewed.
Wear rates are empirical depths per cycle, not Archard coefficients borrowed
from another contact mechanism. Fracture, corrosion and thermal fatigue need
their own supported damage models before an overall mold-life rating exists.

fluid: optional CoolProp result for fluid_requests(spec,s)[0]; when given, real_* metrics are added
beside (never instead of) the existing ideal/assumed-property metrics.

definitions.name: _worker_env
definitions.documentation:
Environment for the worker interpreter. The studio may itself run under the pinned FreeCAD
Python, whose launcher exports PYTHONHOME/PYTHONPATH; inherited by the venv interpreter those
point it at the wrong standard library ("No module named encodings"). Strip them (2026-09-22).

definitions.name: interpreter
definitions.documentation: Return the worker interpreter path, or None when the venv is absent.

definitions.name: handle
definitions.documentation: Run one worker op and return its result, or raise ValueError with the reason.

definitions.name: status
definitions.documentation: Interpreter presence plus rdkit/tblite versions, cached per process.

definitions.name: _mol_elements
definitions.documentation: Element composition {El: n} of a chem.molecule dict (from its atoms).

definitions.name: _match_species
definitions.documentation:
Map a molecule's element composition to a thermo species key (or None).

Prefers the requested phase, then the gas phase, then any match. Elements are
compared as dicts so Hill-order differences in formula strings never matter.

definitions.name: _explicit_smiles
definitions.documentation:
RDKit SMILES with explicit H, so bare-element SMILES ('O' = water) are not
re-read by ``chem.molecule`` as a single atom. Local and deterministic.

definitions.name: _molecule_view
definitions.documentation: chem.molecule dict for the 3D/Lewis view of a species (best effort).

definitions.name: _bond_types
definitions.documentation: Count bonds of each type ('H-H', 'O=O', ...) in a chem.molecule dict.

definitions.name: _diatomic_bond_enthalpy
definitions.signature: e1: str, e2: str, T: float
definitions.documentation:
Mean bond enthalpy (kJ/mol) for an element pair, from the cited database.

Looks for a gas-phase diatomic species with exactly that element composition
and reports its atomization enthalpy X-Y -> X + Y (derived from the cited
formation enthalpies). Returns a value record or None when no such species exists.

definitions.name: _direct_reaction
definitions.signature: feed_counts: dict, product_amounts: dict, T: float
definitions.documentation:
Balanced direct reaction feed -> dominant products, as a thermo.reaction result.

``product_amounts`` are equilibrium moles of the newly formed species. For a
single product the integer coefficient is solved from the element balance
(2 H -> H2); otherwise near-integer amounts are rounded.

definitions.name: _enumerate_xtb
definitions.documentation:
Small valence-saturated molecules from the available atoms (<= 6 heavy atoms),
estimated with GFN2-xTB and separated from the cited equilibrium.

A modest deterministic enumeration: all diatomics of the present elements plus a
curated list of common small molecules whose elements are available. Molecules
already in the cited database (``known_elements``, by element composition) are
skipped.

definitions.name: react
definitions.signature: items, T: float=298.15, P_bar: float=1.0, phase: str='gas', use_xtb: bool=False
definitions.documentation:
Run the My Lab bench: parse items, equilibrate, report products and reaction.

Parameters
----------
items : list[str] | str
    Atom/molecule list, e.g. ``["2 H2", "O2"]`` (count prefixes and comma
    separation accepted; see ``chem.parse_items``).
T : float
    Temperature in K.
P_bar : float
    Total pressure in bar (gas phase).
phase : str
    ``'gas'`` restricts the candidate pool to gas species; anything else also
    allows condensed species (pure phases, activity 1).
use_xtb : bool
    If True, additionally enumerate small valence-saturated molecules and
    estimate them with GFN2-xTB (returned separately, never mixed into the
    cited equilibrium).

definitions.name: _davies_g
definitions.documentation: sqrt(I)/(1+sqrt(I)) - 0.3 I — the Davies ionic-strength factor.

definitions.name: apparent_pkas
definitions.documentation: Temperature- and ionic-strength-corrected pKa ladder for one buffer entry.

definitions.name: _species
definitions.documentation: Fractional populations, average charge and per-step pKa' at a pH.

definitions.name: _mw
definitions.documentation: Molecular weight (g/mol) from a chemical formula (no parentheses), standard atomic weights.

definitions.name: henderson_hasselbalch
definitions.documentation: Henderson-Hasselbalch on the pKa step nearest the stated pH (or invert to find pH from a ratio).

definitions.name: prepare_buffer
definitions.signature: buffer, pH, conc_M, volume_L, form='acid+conjugate', T_C=25.0, I=None, titrant_M=1.0
definitions.documentation: Masses (and titrant volumes) to prepare a buffer; Davies-corrected pKa at the stated ionic strength.

definitions.name: titration
definitions.signature: buffer, conc_M=0.1, I=None, T_C=25.0, ph_range=(1.0, 13.0), points=121
definitions.documentation: Polyprotic titration curve: average charge (equivalents) and buffer capacity vs pH.

definitions.name: ionic_strength
definitions.documentation: I = 0.5 * sum(conc * z^2) over a list of solutes {conc, charge} (or a name->dict map).

definitions.name: pI
definitions.documentation: Isoelectric point: the pH where the net charge of a molecule/peptide crosses zero (bisection).

definitions.name: dG0prime_table
definitions.documentation: The small standard transformed dG' table (pH 7, 25 C); unverified bibliographic values.

definitions.name: dG0prime
definitions.documentation: Look up one standard transformed dG' by id (raises KeyError if unknown).

definitions.name: biochemical_dG
definitions.documentation: dG' = dG'0 + RT ln Q, with Q = [products]/[reactants].

definitions.name: fit_michaelis_menten
definitions.documentation:
Fit a kinetic model by nonlinear least squares; report parameters + SEs/95 % CIs, R^2, AIC,
residuals, and the three linearised plots (Lineweaver-Burk, Eadie-Hofstee, Hanes-Woolf).

definitions.name: _units_for
definitions.documentation: Return the display unit for a fitted parameter.

definitions.name: compare_models
definitions.documentation: Fit every applicable model and return them sorted by AIC (a convenience for model choice).

definitions.name: simulate
definitions.documentation: Integrate a progress curve (scipy solve_ivp). model 'mm' or 'product_inhibition'.

definitions.name: kcat_efficiency
definitions.documentation: Catalytic efficiency kcat/Km and its comparison to the diffusion-controlled limit.

definitions.name: arrhenius_eyring
definitions.documentation: Arrhenius (Ea, ln A) and Eyring (dH#, dS#, dG# at 298.15 K) analysis with CODATA constants.

definitions.name: _clean
definitions.documentation: Strip whitespace and uppercase; return the bare sequence string.

definitions.name: _detect_kind
definitions.documentation: Resolve 'auto' to 'dna'/'rna' or validate an explicit kind.

definitions.name: _validate
definitions.documentation: Validate the sequence against the IUPAC alphabet for its kind; raise with a clear reason.

definitions.name: _reverse_complement
definitions.documentation: Reverse complement via Biopython (exact; complement table includes ambiguity codes).

definitions.name: _gc_percent
definitions.documentation: GC % over the four canonical bases (ambiguity codes excluded from the denominator).

definitions.name: _molecular_weights
definitions.documentation: ss/ds molecular weight (g/mol) via Biopython; unambiguous sequences only.

definitions.name: _extinction
definitions.documentation: Nearest-neighbour epsilon260 (L mol^-1 cm^-1) for a single strand (U treated as T).

definitions.name: _tm_nn
definitions.documentation: Nearest-neighbour Tm (deg C) via Biopython Tm_NN; DNA table for DNA, DNA table on U->T for RNA.

definitions.name: _tm_primer3
definitions.documentation: primer3 calc_tm (deg C) at its defaults (Breslauer NN); DNA only.

definitions.name: _transcribe
definitions.documentation: DNA -> RNA transcript (T -> U); RNA passes through unchanged.

definitions.name: _translate
definitions.documentation: Translate with the standard code, suppressing Biopython's partial-codon warning.

definitions.name: _translate_frame
definitions.documentation: Translate one frame (0-based offset) with the standard code; returns AA string (X for ambiguity).

definitions.name: _orfs
definitions.documentation: ORFs >= min_codons codons in all 6 frames (standard code). Returns a sorted list of dicts.

definitions.name: _aa_of
definitions.documentation: Amino acid for one codon (standard code); '*' for stop, 'X' for ambiguous/short.

definitions.name: _codon_usage
definitions.documentation: Codon and amino-acid counts over a coding region (no partial final codon).

definitions.name: analyze
definitions.documentation: Full nucleic-acid analysis. Returns a dict of cite records plus the 6-frame ORF map.

definitions.name: primers
definitions.documentation:
Design primer pairs with primer3 against a template; report Tm, GC, product size, penalties,
and hairpin/homodimer/heterodimer free energies from primer3's own secondary-structure calls.

definitions.name: _dimer_warnings
definitions.documentation: Warn when any self/hetero dimer is stably folded (|dG| > 6 kcal/mol, a common rule of thumb).

definitions.name: restriction
definitions.documentation:
Restriction sites and fragment sizes via Bio.Restriction; return a site list and a
virtual-gel fragment table (log-size positions for the page).

definitions.name: _fragments
definitions.documentation: Fragment sizes (bp) from sorted cut positions, descending (gel-like order).

definitions.name: align
definitions.documentation: Pairwise alignment with stated scoring; identity % and a formatted (capped) alignment.

definitions.name: _format_alignment
definitions.documentation: Wrap a three-line alignment text into <= cap columns.

definitions.name: mutate
definitions.documentation: Apply point substitutions/insertions/deletions and report the translated consequence.

definitions.name: _Uncovered
definitions.documentation: A molecule (or atom) is outside the groups the Joback table covers.

definitions.name: _is_element_symbol
definitions.documentation: True when `q` is a bare element symbol (H, O, Na, Cl, ...).

definitions.name: _bonds
definitions.documentation: List of (neighbor atom, bond order) for one atom.

definitions.name: _classify
definitions.documentation:
Map one heavy atom to a Joback group key; returns (key, extra_consumed_idx).

Raises _Uncovered when the atom (or a multi-atom group it leads) is outside
the Joback table. `extra_consumed_idx` are neighbor atoms swallowed by a
multi-atom group (carbonyl oxygens, the N of a nitrile, ...) so they are not
double-counted. Callers iterate atoms in ascending atomic number so the
claiming atom always precedes the atoms it claims.

definitions.name: _joback
definitions.documentation:
Joback-Reid group-contribution estimates, or {available: False, reason: ...}.

`mol` is the sanitized molecule (implicit hydrogens). Iterating heavy atoms
in ascending atomic number guarantees the claiming atom of a multi-atom
group (carbonyl C, nitro N, nitrile C) is processed before the atoms it
consumes, so carbonyl/nitro oxygens are never double-counted.

definitions.name: _lewis
definitions.documentation:
Lewis electron bookkeeping from a Kekulized, explicit-H molecule.

Per atom: formal charge q = V - lone - unpaired - bond_order_sum, so
lone_electrons = V - unpaired - bond_order_sum - q (V = outer-shell
electrons). Aromatic bonds are Kekulized first so heteroaromatic atoms get
integer bond orders (furan O -> 2 single bonds -> 2 lone pairs).

definitions.name: _lewis_text
definitions.documentation: One plain-English sentence explaining the electron picture.

definitions.name: _embed_3d
definitions.documentation:
Embed 3D coordinates: ETKDG (randomSeed=0xf00d) then MMFF (UFF fallback).

Single atoms sit at the origin; diatomics are aligned along +z at the
force-field bond length. Returns the optimization method name (or None).

definitions.name: _from_mol
definitions.documentation: Assemble the full molecule dict from a parsed, sanitized RDKit Mol.

definitions.name: _detect_groups
definitions.documentation: Sorted list of functional-group names matched by SMARTS on the heavy-atom mol.

definitions.name: molecule
definitions.documentation:
Resolve a query (element symbol / SMILES / name) into a molecule dict.

See module docstring for the detection order and the returned structure.
Numeric properties are cite.value records; structural integers are plain.

definitions.name: parse_items
definitions.documentation:
Split a reactant list into counted molecules.

Each item may carry a count: "2 H", "2H" (leading number) or "O2 x3"
(trailing "xN"). A single comma-separated string is accepted too. Returns
[{"count": n, "molecule": molecule(q)}].

definitions.name: _pubchem_by_inchikey
definitions.documentation:
SMILES for an InChIKey from PubChem's inchikey endpoint (the name endpoint does not accept keys).

Cached under <data>/records/inchikey_<KEY>.json so a repeat resolve is offline and reproducible.

definitions.name: _from_pubchem
definitions.documentation: PubChem-backed resolution (cached); returns a result dict or None when nothing matched.

definitions.name: resolve

Resolve any notation to {smiles, via, input, normalised, …}; raises ValueError with the reason.

`smiles` is the canonical isomeric SMILES — the identity every science toolkit run keys on.
`via` names the rule that fired: prefix:<kind>, inchi, inchikey, cas, common_formula, smiles,
formula_pubchem or name_pubchem.

definitions.documentation: Lazily build the atom-pair *count* fingerprint generator (fixed options).

definitions.name: canonical_json
