coverage: Packaged implementation; no direct test reference found.

definitions.name: _clist
definitions.documentation: Sorted [real, imag] pairs from a sequence of complex roots/values (deterministic order).

definitions.name: _tf
definitions.documentation: Coefficient lists with leading zeros stripped; denominator must be non-degenerate.

definitions.name: _phase_sweep
definitions.documentation:
Continuous (unwrapped) phase of G(jω) = N(jω)/D(jω): sum of zero angles minus pole angles.

Each term atan2(ω − Im c, −Re c) is the angle of the vector from a pole/zero c to the point jω on
the imaginary axis; summing them (np.roots carries multiplicity) yields a continuous phase that keeps
decreasing through −180° instead of wrapping, unlike the principal angle np.angle. The sign of the
(real) leading coefficient contributes ±π.

definitions.name: _lead_sign
definitions.documentation: Sign of a polynomial p(ε) for small ε > 0: the sign of its lowest-degree non-zero coefficient.

definitions.name: _sign_limit
definitions.documentation: Sign of a Routh first-column entry in the limit ε → 0⁺ (sign of its leading ε term).

definitions.name: _as_float
definitions.documentation: Finite float limit of a Routh entry as ε → 0⁺ (None where it diverges), for JSON display.

definitions.name: _poles_zeros
definitions.documentation: Poles, zeros and DC gain of G(s) = num/den via scipy.signal.tf2zpk, plus the system type.

definitions.name: _block
definitions.documentation: Block-diagram reduction of two transfer functions (series, parallel, feedback).

definitions.name: _ss_error
definitions.documentation:
System type, static error constants and steady-state errors from the open-loop G(s) = num/den.

Type N = number of poles at the origin (trailing zero coefficients in den). With K = N(0)/D_red(0):
Kp = K (N=0) else ∞; Kv = 0 (N=0), K (N=1), ∞ (N≥2); Ka = 0 (N≤1), K (N=2), ∞ (N>2). Steady-state
errors: e_step = 1/(1+Kp); e_ramp = 1/Kv; e_para = 1/Ka. An infinite error is reported as null.

definitions.name: _routh
definitions.documentation:
Routh–Hurwitz stability of the characteristic polynomial (descending coefficients).

Builds the Routh array exactly (sympy rationals). A zero first-column entry with a non-zero row is
replaced by ε and the first column is read in the limit ε → 0⁺; an all-zero row is replaced by the
derivative of the auxiliary polynomial and signals marginal stability (roots on the imaginary axis).
Sign changes in the first column equal the number of right-half-plane roots.

definitions.name: _freq_response
definitions.documentation: Magnitude (linear and dB) and continuous phase of G(jω) at one frequency.

definitions.name: _root_locus
definitions.documentation: Closed-loop poles of 1 + K G(s) = 0 at a given gain K (den + K·num = 0).

definitions.name: _stability_margins
definitions.documentation:
Gain margin (dB), phase margin (rad), crossover frequencies and closed-loop bandwidth.

Gain crossover ω_gc: |G| = 1 (0 dB); phase margin = π + ∠G(jω_gc) with the continuous (unwrapped)
phase, so an already-unstable loop gives a negative margin. Phase crossover ω_pc: Im G crosses zero
with Re G < 0 (∠G = −180°); gain margin = −20 log10 |G(jω_pc)|. A phase pinned at −180° (e.g. a
double integrator 1/s²) has no genuine crossing, so those margins are null. Bandwidth: first ω where
the closed loop T = G/(1+G) = N/(D+N) falls 3.0103 dB below its DC gain (null for zero/infinite DC).

definitions.name: _pid_zn
definitions.documentation:
PID/P/PI gains by the closed-loop (ultimate-gain) Ziegler–Nichols rules from K_u and T_u.

Variant: ultimate-sensitivity (Ziegler–Nichols, 1942). P: Kp = 0.5 K_u. PI: Kp = 0.45 K_u,
Ti = T_u/1.2. PID: Kp = 0.6 K_u, Ti = T_u/2, Td = T_u/8 (parallel form Ki = Kp/Ti, Kd = Kp·Td).

definitions.name: _state_space
definitions.documentation:
Poles and controllability/observability of ẋ = A x + B u, y = C x.

Controllability matrix [B, AB, …, A^(n−1)B]; observability matrix [C; CA; …; CA^(n−1)]. Full rank ⇔
controllable/observable. The feedthrough matrix D does not affect any of these quantities.

imports: from engineering_sim.science.mech.core import Calc, MechError, V, section
coverage: Packaged implementation; no direct test reference found.

definitions.name: MechError
definitions.documentation: User-facing calculator error (bad input, unsolvable request); message is shown verbatim.

definitions.name: Var
definitions.documentation:
One calculator variable.

name     identifier used in equations/procedures (ASCII, e.g. 'sigma_x', 'T1')
unit     coherent SI pint unit string; '' for dimensionless
desc     one-line meaning shown in the form
lo, hi   admissible SI range (inclusive); roots outside are rejected; also brackets numeric solves
label    display symbol (unicode), defaults to name
integer  True for counts (teeth, coils); solved values are reported with a rounding warning
signed   True when negative values are physical (moments, deflections); default False means >=0
         unless ``lo`` says otherwise
source   optional cite record dict for a coefficient whose default is taken from a table
kind     'scalar' (default), 'json' for structured procedure inputs (truss geometry, part lists) or
         'text' for a string such as a fluid name or end condition (optionally restricted to ``choices``);
         json/text values pass through unconverted (state SI units of json in ``desc``) and are never
         solved for

definitions.name: V
definitions.documentation: Shorthand constructor used by section modules: V('P', 'N', 'axial load').

definitions.name: Calc
definitions.documentation:
One calculator. Exactly one of ``equations`` / ``procedure`` is set.

key          short id inside the section ('belt_friction'); full id is '<section>.<key>'
title        human title
vars         list[Var] covering every symbol used
outputs      default unknowns (equation calcs) or produced values (procedures)
equations    list of 'lhs = rhs' strings
procedure    callable(dict name->float SI) -> dict name->float (or list/dict structures)
example      dict name->SI float for every non-output variable (physically sensible case)
assumptions  list of strings (validity limits the user must know)
refs         list of strings: standard textbook relation names / standards. Recalled references are
             labelled as such; never invent page numbers.
plots        list of plot specs: {'id','title','x','y':[...],'from','to','n','xlog','ylog'} for a generic
             sweep, or {'id','title','fn': callable(values)->chart} for a custom diagram
keywords     extra search terms
no_invert    {var: reason} for variables that cannot be recovered (e.g. appears only inside a floor())

definitions.name: registry
definitions.documentation: {'sections': {key: Section}, 'calcs': {id: Calc}}; loaded once per process, sorted by order.

definitions.name: unit_of
definitions.documentation: pint Unit for a declared unit string ('' -> dimensionless).

definitions.name: to_si
definitions.documentation:
Convert user input (number | '12 kN' | {'value','unit'}) to a float in var.unit.

A bare number is taken to be in the declared unit. Offset temperatures ('20 degC') are handled by
building the Quantity from (magnitude, unit) rather than multiplying, which pint forbids.

definitions.name: _radian_power
definitions.documentation: Exponent of radian in the root units (rpm → rad/s has 1; Hz → 1/s has 0).

definitions.name: _check_angle_content
definitions.documentation:
Reject cyclic ↔ angular mix-ups that pint would silently convert with a 2π error.

pint defines revolution = 2π rad and treats rad as dimensionless, so '1500 rpm' → 157 1/s and
'1 Hz' → 1 rad/s. mechcalc therefore requires angular quantities (ω, θ) to be declared in rad-based
units and cyclic ones (f, n in Hz or 1/s) not to be, and refuses inputs whose radian content differs.

definitions.name: from_si
definitions.documentation: Convert an SI float to the requested display unit (returns value, unit).

definitions.name: _ck
definitions.documentation: Cache key: id plus object identity, so two declarations sharing an id never share symbols.

definitions.name: symbols
definitions.documentation: {name: sympy Symbol}; real symbols, positive when the variable cannot be negative.

definitions.name: parsed
definitions.documentation: List of sympy Eq objects for an equation calculator (cached).

definitions.name: time_limit
definitions.documentation:
SIGALRM guard around sympy.solve, which can run unboundedly on transcendental systems.

Only effective in the main thread (worker and unittest both qualify); elsewhere it is a no-op.

definitions.name: general_solution
definitions.documentation:
Closed-form solutions for ``unknowns`` in terms of the other variables, or None.

Returns a list of dicts {unknown: lambdified function(*known_values)} plus the ordered known names.
Cached; a timeout or NotImplementedError caches None so numeric fallback is used immediately.

definitions.name: _abs_terms
definitions.documentation:
Cancellation-free magnitude of an expression: every sum becomes a sum of absolute values.

Used only to scale residuals: when terms cancel to (near) zero — a radial stress at a free edge, a
holding force exactly at the friction limit — round-off is judged against the size of the cancelling
terms instead of against zero. Functions such as exp/cos keep their arguments unchanged.

definitions.name: residual_fn
definitions.documentation:
Signed, scale-free residuals: f(values dict) -> [(lhs - rhs) / scale, ...].

scale = max(|lhs|, |rhs|, 1e-6 · (|lhs|_terms + |rhs|_terms)); with the 1e-7 acceptance
threshold a root must satisfy the equation to 1e-13 of its cancelling-term magnitude with |·|_terms from _abs_terms, so the
residual is relative for ordinary values yet smooth and meaningful when a side is legitimately zero.

definitions.name: _numeric_bits
definitions.documentation: Approximate size in bits of an exact sympy number (0 for floats/symbolic), without evaluating powers.

definitions.name: safe_expr
definitions.documentation:
Build a sympy expression from user text WITHOUT evaluating any Python.

The text is parsed with ``ast.parse(mode='eval')`` and only these nodes are accepted: numeric constants,
names (declared ``variables``, allow-listed constants), + − × ÷ ** % and unary ±, ``^`` (rewritten to **)
and calls of allow-listed function names with positional arguments. Attribute access, subscripts,
lambdas, comprehensions, strings, keywords and every other node raise MechError, so payloads such as
``().__class__.__mro__`` cannot run. Constant exponents above ``max_exponent`` are refused (DoS guard).
Returns (expr, {name: Symbol}) with real symbols for the declared variables.

definitions.name: _dimensionless_special
definitions.documentation: Stand-in for a special function during the dimension check: argument must be dimensionless.

definitions.name: dimension_check
definitions.documentation:
Return a list of problems (empty = consistent). Equation calcs only.

Each variable is replaced by a pint Quantity of its declared unit (magnitude 1.37 to keep log/asin
arguments in-domain for most relations) and both sides of every equation are evaluated. pint raises
on adding incompatible terms or passing a dimensioned value to exp/log/sin; the two sides must then
share one dimensionality.

definitions.name: _real
definitions.documentation: Real float from a numpy/sympy/complex scalar, or None when genuinely complex/non-finite.

definitions.name: _scan_grid
definitions.documentation: Candidate abscissae for a 1-D root scan inside the variable's admissible range.

definitions.name: _numeric_1d
definitions.documentation: All sign-change roots of scalar f over grid, refined by brentq. f may return None (domain error).

definitions.name: solve_equations
definitions.documentation:
Solve an equation calculator. known: {name: SI float}; returns (solutions, method).

solutions is a list of dicts over ``unknowns`` (admissible, verified by residual), sorted so the
first is closest (log-distance) to the calculator's example values — a deterministic, physically
typical choice when a relation has several roots (quadratics, inverse trig).

definitions.name: _numeric_solve
definitions.documentation:
Fallback solver. Sequential decomposition first: repeatedly take an equation with exactly one
remaining unknown, find all its bracketed roots in 1-D and branch on each; any coupled remainder goes
to bounded multi-start least squares. Branching keeps every admissible root, not just the first.

definitions.name: _least_squares
definitions.documentation:
Bounded multi-start least squares on normalized residuals (coupled systems and procedures).

Starts: the example values, then deterministic log-uniform spreads clipped into each variable's
admissible range, so the optimiser never wanders into physically excluded regions.

definitions.name: run_procedure
definitions.documentation:
Procedure calculators: forward when every unknown is an output; else numeric inversion.

Inversion: the caller supplies target values for as many outputs as there are unknown inputs; the
remaining outputs are then computed forward at the recovered inputs.

definitions.name: _clean
definitions.documentation: JSON-safe structure: non-finite floats become None (the worker refuses NaN/inf).

definitions.name: parse_inputs
definitions.documentation: User inputs -> SI floats; unknown variables are ignored even if a value was sent.

definitions.name: compute
definitions.documentation: Solve one calculator and return the full provenance-carrying result dict.

definitions.name: _format
definitions.signature: calc, known, unknowns, sols, method, out_units

definitions.name: equation_text
definitions.documentation: [{'text','latex'}] for display. Procedures show their declared relation summary in refs instead.

definitions.name: display_value
definitions.documentation: Readable metric (value, unit) for an SI value: the suggested unit giving 1 ≤ |v| < 1000 (angles in deg).

definitions.name: describe
definitions.documentation: Form schema for one calculator.

definitions.name: catalog
definitions.documentation: Sections with their calculators, optionally filtered by free-text query.

definitions.name: sweep
definitions.signature: calc_id, inputs, var, start, stop, n=50, solve_for=None, log=False, out_units=None
definitions.documentation: Vary one known input over [start, stop] and tabulate the unknowns; returns table + chart spec.

definitions.name: plot
definitions.documentation: Named plot declared by the calculator: generic sweep spec or custom diagram function.

definitions.name: example_solution
definitions.documentation: Full SI assignment of every variable at the calculator's example (forward solve).

definitions.name: roundtrip
definitions.documentation:
Recover every invertible variable from the others at the example point.

Equation calcs: for each variable v, try unknown sets formed by swapping v in for one output; the
check passes when the original value is among the admissible roots. Procedures: each scalar input
is recovered against one scalar output target. Returns {var: 'ok' | 'skipped: reason' | 'FAIL: ...'}.

coverage: Test-text reference only; not measured branch/function coverage.

definitions.name: _refrigeration_tons
definitions.documentation: Cooling capacity in watts from tons of refrigeration (1 ton = 3.51685 kW, ASHRAE).

definitions.name: _otto_full
definitions.documentation:
Air-standard Otto cycle per unit mass of working fluid (constant cv, cp).

States: 1 BDC before compression, 2 TDC after isentropic compression, 3 after constant-volume heat
addition q_in, 4 after isentropic expansion back to V1. Returns temperatures (K), pressures (Pa),
net work (J/kg), thermal efficiency and mean effective pressure (Pa).

definitions.name: _reheat_turbine
definitions.documentation:
Two-stage ideal-gas turbine with reheat to T_max between the stages.

a = (γ−1)/γ; T2s = T_max (P_int/P1)^a is the exit of stage 1, T4s = T_max (P2/P_int)^a of stage 2
(both reheated to T_max at entry). w_single is the work of one turbine expanding P1 → P2 with no
reheat, so w_extra is the work gained by reheating. Equal stage pressure ratios (P_int = sqrt(P1 P2))
maximise w_two for a given T_max.

definitions.name: _vc_states
definitions.documentation:
Ideal vapour-compression states for one stage (isentropic compressor, throttling valve).

Returns dict with sat_evap (saturation at evaporator), sat_cond (saturation at condenser),
h1 = saturated-vapour enthalpy at P_evap, s1, h3 = saturated-liquid enthalpy at P_cond,
h4 = h3 (throttling), h2s = isentropic-compression outlet enthalpy at P_cond. All SI.

definitions.name: _vapor_compression
definitions.documentation:
Single-stage vapour-compression refrigeration cycle.

States: 1 saturated vapour at the evaporator, 2 compressor outlet (isentropic to P_cond), 3 saturated
liquid at the condenser, 4 throttled to the evaporator (h4 = h3). Refrigeration effect per kg is
q_L = h1 − h4; compressor work per kg is w_c = h2s − h1 (ideal). With the mass-flow rate m_dot the
capacity is Q_dot = m_dot q_L and the compressor power W_dot = m_dot w_c; COP = q_L / w_c.

definitions.name: _turbine_inlet
definitions.documentation:
Turbine-inlet state: saturated vapour at T_sat(P_boiler) or superheated steam at T_boiler.

Returns (h, s, T_sat). Raises MechError when T_boiler is meaningfully below the saturation
temperature (a subcooled/two-phase turbine inlet) and when P_boiler has no saturation point
(above the fluid critical pressure — supercritical cycles are not modelled).

definitions.name: _rankine
definitions.documentation:
Ideal (or actual) Rankine cycle from CoolProp state points.

States: 1 saturated liquid at P_cond, 2 pump outlet (h2 = h1 + v1 ΔP / η_pump), 3 turbine inlet —
saturated vapour at P_boiler when T_boiler ≈ T_sat(P_boiler), otherwise superheated to T_boiler —,
4 turbine outlet (h4 = h3 − η_turb (h3 − h4s), h4s at P_cond with s = s3). Returns the state
enthalpies, quality at the turbine outlet, works, heats, and thermal efficiency.

definitions.name: _rankine_reheat
definitions.documentation:
Reheat Rankine cycle.

1 sat. liquid at P_cond → 2 pump to P_boiler → 3 superheat to T_boiler at P_boiler → 4 HP turbine to
P_reheat (s constant) → 5 reheat to T_reheat at P_reheat → 6 LP turbine to P_cond → 1. The HP/LP
turbines share one isentropic efficiency η_turb; the pump uses η_pump. Returns enthalpy at every
state, works, heats, LP-turbine-exit quality x6, and thermal efficiency.

definitions.name: _rankine_regenerative
definitions.documentation:
Regenerative Rankine with one open feedwater heater (OFWH).

1 sat. liquid at P_cond → 2 pump I to P_fwh → mixed with extraction flow y at P_fwh → 3 sat. liquid at
P_fwh → 4 pump II to P_boiler → 5 turbine inlet (sat. vapour at P_boiler or superheated to T_boiler) →
6 extraction at P_fwh, 7 turbine exit at P_cond. The extraction mass fraction y follows from the OFWH
energy balance y h6 + (1−y) h2 = h3. The turbine isentropic efficiency η_turb is applied to both
stages: h6 = h5 − η_turb(h5 − h6s), s6 = s(P_fwh, h6), then h7 = h6 − η_turb(h6 − h7s) with
h7s = h(P_cond, s6). Works are per unit mass through the boiler/turbine.

definitions.name: _cascade
definitions.documentation:
Two-stage cascade refrigeration cycle (one working fluid in both stages).

Low stage evaporates at P_evap and condenses at P_cascade; high stage evaporates at P_cascade and
condenses at P_cond. The cascade exchanger balances heat: ṁ_high / ṁ_low = (h2 − h3)_low / (h1 − h4)_high.
COP and specific heats/works are per unit mass of low-stage refrigerant.

definitions.name: _multistage
definitions.documentation:
Two-stage vapour-compression with a flash chamber (multistage refrigeration).

1 sat. vapour at P_evap → 2 isentropic compression to P_int; the condenser liquid (5, sat. liquid at
P_cond) is throttled to P_int (state 6, quality x6) and separated in the flash chamber into sat.
vapour (3) and sat. liquid (7 → evaporator). Vapour flows mix (m1 h2 + m3 h3 = m2 h8) before the
second-stage compression 8 → 9 to P_cond. COP and works are per unit mass through the evaporator.

definitions.name: _tolerance_stackup
definitions.documentation: Worst-case and RSS (statistical) tolerance stack of dimensions [[nominal, +/-tol], ...].

definitions.name: _renard_series
definitions.documentation: Unrounded Renard preferred numbers of series R(n) over one decade: 10^(i/n) for i = 0..n-1.

imports: from engineering_sim.science.mech.core import Calc, MechError, V, section
coverage: Packaged implementation; no direct test reference found.

definitions.name: _number
definitions.documentation: Coerce a JSON scalar to a finite float, or raise MechError (never a bare ValueError).

definitions.name: _polish_root
definitions.documentation:
Refine a real root x0 of the NPV polynomial P (in x = 1 + r) to machine precision.

A simple root is bracketed on P itself (sign change). A tangent/even-multiplicity root does not
change sign in P, so it is bracketed on the derivative P′ (which has a simple root there).

definitions.name: _irr
definitions.documentation:
All real internal rates of return from a cash-flow list [CF0, CF1, ...].

NPV(r) = Σ CF_t (1+r)^-t. Multiplying by (1+r)^(n-1) turns this into a polynomial in x = 1 + r with
the cash flows as coefficients, so numpy.roots gives every root (including tangent/even-multiplicity
roots and rates near −100 %); each real x > 0 is polished against the polynomial directly (evaluated
by Horner in x to avoid the cancellation the sum Σ CF_t/(1+r)^t suffers near a multiple root).

definitions.name: _depreciation_table
definitions.documentation: Depreciation from a user-supplied percentage schedule (e.g. MACRS rates).

definitions.name: _annual_worth
definitions.documentation: Annual worth from a present amount (capital-recovery factor), with the i = 0 limit A = P/n.

definitions.name: _sinking_fund
definitions.documentation: Annual deposit to accumulate a future sum (sinking-fund factor), with the i = 0 limit A = F/n.

definitions.name: _life_cycle_cost
definitions.documentation: Life-cycle cost (present worth) with the i = 0 limit LCC = C0 + n·C_annual.

definitions.name: _depreciation_sl
definitions.documentation: Straight-line depreciation D = (P − S)/n and book value, with k > n rejected.

definitions.name: _depreciation_soyd
definitions.documentation: Sum-of-years-digits depreciation and book value, with k > n rejected.

definitions.name: _cash_flow_series

imports: from engineering_sim.science.mech.core import Calc, MechError, V, section
coverage: Packaged implementation; no direct test reference found.

definitions.name: _dc_motor
definitions.documentation:
Steady-state permanent-magnet / separately-excited DC model: V = I·R + ke·ω, T = kt·I.

Adds the back EMF E = ke·ω, the no-load speed ω_nl = V/ke (T = 0) and the stall torque
T_stall = kt·V/R (ω = 0). T above the stall torque would need ω < 0 and raises MechError; a
mismatch between kt and ke is surfaced as a warning (they are equal in coherent SI for an ideal
machine).

definitions.name: _encoder
definitions.documentation: Quadrature encoder resolution; the decoding multiplier m is restricted to 1, 2 or 4.

imports: from engineering_sim.science.mech.core import Calc, MechError, V, section
coverage: Packaged implementation; no direct test reference found.

definitions.name: _niosh
definitions.documentation:
Revised NIOSH lifting equation (metric): RWL = LC·HM·VM·DM·AM·FM·CM, LI = Load/RWL.

Multiplier bounds (NIOSH safety limits): HM = 25/H capped at 1 for H < 25 cm and 0 for H > 63 cm;
VM = 1 − 0.003|V − 75|, zero for V > 175 cm; DM = 0.82 + 4.5/D capped at 1 for D < 25 cm (D = 0 is
allowed) and 0 for D > 175 cm; AM = 1 − 0.0032·A, zero for A > 135° (H, V, D in cm, A in degrees).

imports: from engineering_sim.science.mech.core import Calc, MechError, V, section
coverage: Packaged implementation; no direct test reference found.

definitions.name: _marin_surface
definitions.documentation:
Surface (Marin) factor ka = a·(Sut/MPa)^b with a, b from the Marin surface table (Sut in MPa).

Example pairs (a, b): ground 1.58, −0.085; machined/cold-drawn 4.51, −0.265; hot-rolled 57.7,
−0.718; as-forged 272, −0.995. These are the user's inputs, not built-in values.

definitions.name: _marin_size
definitions.documentation:
Size (Marin) factor kb for a rotating round section (d in mm).

kb = 1.24 d^−0.107 for 2.79 ≤ d ≤ 51 mm; kb = 1.51 d^−0.157 for 51 < d ≤ 254 mm. Axial load gives
kb = 1 regardless of size (enter it directly in the corrected-endurance calculator).

definitions.name: _sn_constants
definitions.documentation: S–N power-law constants a, b from two points: S = a·N^b (b = ln(S1/S2)/ln(N1/N2)).

definitions.name: _miner
definitions.documentation: Miner's linear cumulative-damage rule: D = Σ n_i/N_i over blocks [[n_i, N_i], ...].

definitions.name: _neuber
definitions.documentation:
Neuber's rule with a Ramberg–Osgood cyclic stress–strain curve, solved by bisection.

Finds the local (notch-root) stress σ and strain ε satisfying the Neuber hyperbola
σ·ε = (Kf·S)²/E together with ε = σ/E + (σ/K')^(1/n'). The nominal stress S is elastic, so the
nominal strain is e = S/E; Kf is the fatigue notch factor (Kt may be used for a sharp elastic notch).

definitions.name: _fatigue_diagram
definitions.documentation: Failure loci in the σm–σa plane (Goodman, Gerber, Soderberg, ASME elliptic, Langer yield).

definitions.name: _endurance_prime
definitions.documentation:
Endurance limit of a steel from Sut: Se′ = 0.5 Sut up to 1400 MPa, capped at 700 MPa above.

The cap applies to steels only; wrought aluminium alloys (Se′ ≈ 0.4 Sut) are not handled here.

definitions.name: _sn_power
definitions.documentation: Fatigue strength S = a·N^b (Basquin power law); warns outside the 10³–10⁶ cycle validity range.

definitions.name: _fatigue_criteria
definitions.documentation:
Goodman, Gerber, Soderberg, ASME-elliptic and Langer factors of safety.

For a compressive mean stress (sigma_m < 0) the mean stress does not reduce fatigue life, so the
four fatigue criteria all reduce to n = Se/sigma_a (the fully-reversed value); the first-cycle-yield
guard becomes n_y = Sy/(sigma_a + |sigma_m|), i.e. Sy/(sigma_a − sigma_m) with sigma_m < 0. The
ASME-elliptic relation is even in sigma_m; treating its compressive branch as non-damaging (the same
Se/sigma_a reduction as Goodman/Gerber/Soderberg) is the documented convention here.

imports: from engineering_sim.science.mech.core import Calc, MechError, V, section
coverage: Packaged implementation; no direct test reference found.

definitions.name: _axial_solve
definitions.documentation:
Assemble and solve a 1-D (spring/bar) system. elements = [(i, j, k_axial)]; fixed = [[node, u]];
loads = [[node, F]]. Returns (K, u, R) with R = K·u − F (support reactions).

definitions.name: _max_node
definitions.documentation:
Number of nodes (max index + 1), validating every index.

``elements`` are the [i, j, ...] rows (two node indices per row); ``node_lists`` are the
[node, ...] rows (fixed/loads/supports, one index per row). A negative index would silently wrap in
numpy (K[-1, -1] indexes the last row/col), and a non-integer index would silently truncate with
int(), so every index is validated here and at each parse site.

definitions.name: _node_idx
definitions.documentation: Validate one node index: an integer in 0..n-1 (or >= 0 when n is None).

definitions.name: _spring_system
definitions.documentation:
1-D spring direct stiffness: springs [[i, j, k (N/m)], ...], fixed [[node, u (m)], ...],
loads [[node, F (N)], ...].

definitions.name: _bar_system
definitions.documentation: 1-D bar (rod) direct stiffness: bars [[i, j, E (Pa), A (m^2), L (m)], ...].

definitions.name: _truss_fea
definitions.documentation:
2-D plane truss by direct stiffness: nodes [[x, y] (m)], elements [[i, j, E (Pa), A (m^2)]],
supports [[node, 'x'|'y']] (zero displacement), loads [[node, Fx, Fy] (N)].

definitions.name: _beam_fea
definitions.documentation:
Euler–Bernoulli beam assembly: elements [[i, j, E (Pa), I (m^4), L (m)]], supports
[[node, 'v'|'theta']] (zero), loads [[node, P (N), M (N·m)]]. 2 DOF per node (v, θ).

definitions.name: _bar_element
definitions.documentation: 1-D bar element stiffness matrix (2×2) and axial stiffness EA/L.

definitions.name: _beam_element
definitions.documentation: Euler–Bernoulli beam element stiffness matrix (4×4, DOF [v_i, θ_i, v_j, θ_j]) and 12EI/L³.

definitions.name: _truss_element_2d
definitions.documentation: 2-D truss element stiffness matrix in global coordinates (4×4) and axial stiffness EA/L.

definitions.name: _fd_heat_1d
definitions.documentation:
Steady 1-D heat conduction with uniform generation by central finite differences.

k d²T/dx² + q = 0 on [0, L], T(0) = T_left, T(L) = T_right; n interior nodes. Central differences are
exact for this constant-source quadratic, so the nodal values equal the closed form
T(x) = T_left + (T_right − T_left)x/L + q·x(L − x)/(2k).

definitions.name: _fd_advection_diffusion
definitions.documentation:
Steady 1-D advection-diffusion u dc/dx = D d²c/dx², c(0)=c0, c(L)=cL, by central finite differences.

n interior nodes; central scheme needs a cell Peclet number |u Δx/D| < 2. The analytic solution is
c(x) = c0 + (cL − c0)(e^(Pe x/L) − 1)/(e^Pe − 1), Pe = uL/D (a convergence landmark, not a re-typed matrix).

imports: from engineering_sim.science.mech.core import Calc, MechError, V, section
coverage: Test-text reference only; not measured branch/function coverage.

definitions.name: _friction_factor
definitions.documentation: Darcy friction factor: laminar 64/Re, Colebrook (iterated), Swamee–Jain and Haaland.

definitions.name: _moody_chart
definitions.documentation: Moody diagram spec: laminar 64/Re plus Colebrook curves for several ε/D, log–log.

definitions.name: _momentum_bend
definitions.documentation:
Force of a steady fluid stream on a pipe bend/nozzle/vane (2-D, horizontal plane).

inlet/outlet are [v (m/s), p (Pa, gauge), A (m²), theta (deg from +x)]; rho (kg/m³). The force is
that exerted BY the fluid ON the bend: F = p1 A1 e1 − p2 A2 e2 + mdot (v1 e1 − v2 e2).

definitions.name: _boundary_layer
definitions.documentation: Flat-plate boundary layer: laminar (Blasius) and turbulent (1/7 power law) thicknesses and C_f.

definitions.name: _buckingham
definitions.documentation:
Buckingham π theorem: dimensionless groups from the dimension matrix via sympy nullspace.

matrix: rows = fundamental dimensions (M, L, T, ...), columns = physical quantities, integer
exponents. The first `rank` columns must be the repeating variables (independent). Each π group is
one non-repeating variable times powers of the repeating variables: solve D_r·a = −d_j for column j.

definitions.name: _series_pipes
definitions.documentation: Total head loss for pipes in series (one flow rate): h = Σ (f L/D + K) V²/(2g).

definitions.name: _pipe_network
definitions.documentation:
Pipe network by the Hardy Cross loop method.

pipes: [[id, L (m), D (m), f, K, Q0 (m³/s)], ...]; initial flows Q0 must satisfy junction
continuity. loops: [[[id, dir], ...], ...] with dir +1/−1 relative to each pipe's positive flow.
Iterates ΔQ = −Σ(dr·R·Q|Q|) / Σ(2·R·|Q|) around each loop until |ΔQ| < 1e-9 m³/s.

imports: from engineering_sim.science.mech.core import Calc, MechError, V, section
coverage: Packaged implementation; no direct test reference found.

definitions.name: _fluid_state_lookup
definitions.documentation: State of a CoolProp fluid from T and P via common.fluid_state (the shared adapter).

definitions.name: _rigid_body_accel
definitions.documentation:
Uniformly accelerating fluid tank: free-surface tilt and pressure at a point.

theta = atan(a_x/(g + a_z)) is the angle of the free-surface normal from vertical toward +x;
p = p_ref − ρ(a_x·x + (g + a_z)·z) with z positive upward and (x, z) measured from the reference point.
Requires g + a_z > 0 — in free fall the free surface does not exist, so that case is rejected.

imports: from engineering_sim.science.mech.core import Calc, MechError, V, section
coverage: Packaged implementation; no direct test reference found.

definitions.name: _paris_growth
definitions.documentation: Paris-law crack growth rate: da/dN = C dK^m, with dK = Y dsigma sqrt(pi a).

definitions.name: _paris_cycles
definitions.documentation:
Cycles to failure under the Paris law with a constant geometry factor Y.

Closed form of N_f = integral_{a0}^{ac} da / (C (Y dsigma sqrt(pi a))^m) for m != 2 and m = 2.

definitions.name: _paris_cycles_ya
definitions.documentation:
Cycles to failure with a crack-length-dependent geometry factor Y(a) given as a table.

N_f = integral_{a0}^{ac} da / (C (Y(a) dsigma sqrt(pi a))^m), with Y(a) linearly interpolated from
Y_table. The integral is evaluated per table segment with scipy.integrate.quad (the integrand is
~a^(-m/2), so a uniform trapezoid is inaccurate; integrating segment-by-segment across the table
breakpoints keeps Y piecewise-linear and the quadrature convergent).

definitions.name: _leak_before_break
definitions.documentation:
Leak-before-break: critical through-wall crack half-length vs wall thickness.

a_c = (K_Ic/(Y sigma))^2 / pi is the critical half-length. A through-wall crack of total length ~2t
(half-length ~t) leaks detectably, so leak-before-break holds when the crack half-length reaches t
before the critical half-length a_c, i.e. margin = a_c/t > 1.

imports: from engineering_sim.science.mech.core import Calc, MechError, V, section
coverage: Packaged implementation; no direct test reference found.

definitions.name: _barth
definitions.documentation:
Barth velocity factor Kv (multiplying form, Kv >= 1) for the Lewis bending path, V in m/s.

Kv_cast   = (3.05 + V)/3.05        cast-iron / cast teeth
Kv_cut    = (6.1 + V)/6.1          cut or milled teeth
Kv_hobbed = (3.56 + sqrt(V))/3.56  hobbed or shaped teeth
Kv_shaved = (5.56 + sqrt(V))/5.56  shaved or ground teeth
The additive constants carry units of m/s (sqrt(V) terms carry sqrt(m/s)), so this is a procedure
(not a dimensional equation). Kv >= 1 multiplies the static Lewis stress: sigma = Kv Wt/(F m Y).

definitions.name: _gear_life_cycles
definitions.documentation: Number of load cycles at speed n (rev/s) over L_h hours: N = L_h * 3600 * n.

imports: from engineering_sim.science.mech.core import Calc, MechError, V, section
coverage: Test-text reference only; not measured branch/function coverage.

definitions.name: _fin_straight
definitions.documentation:
Straight rectangular fin with a convective tip (exact solution).

P = 2(w + t), A_c = w·t, m = sqrt(hP/(kA_c)). The exact convective-tip heat rate is
Q = sqrt(hPkA_c)·θ_b·(sinh(mL) + (h/mk)cosh(mL)) / (cosh(mL) + (h/mk)sinh(mL)); efficiency
η = Q/(h A_f θ_b) with A_f = P·L + A_c (side area plus tip face); effectiveness
ε = Q/(h A_c θ_b); tip temperature from the exact profile θ_tip/θ_b = 1/(cosh(mL) + (h/mk)sinh(mL)).

definitions.name: _one_term_plane
definitions.documentation:
First-term (Fo > 0.2) transient solution for a plane wall of half-thickness L in convection.

Eigenvalue ζ1 solves ζ tan ζ = Bi on (0, π/2); C1 = 4 sin ζ1/(2ζ1 + sin 2ζ1). Centre and surface
temperatures follow θ = C1 exp(-ζ1² Fo) cos(ζ1 x/L).

definitions.name: _one_term_cylinder
definitions.documentation:
First-term (Fo > 0.2) transient solution for an infinite cylinder of radius r0 in convection.

Eigenvalue ζ1 solves ζ J1(ζ)/J0(ζ) = Bi on (0, 2.4048); C1 = 2 J1(ζ)/(ζ (J0² + J1²)). Centre and
surface temperatures follow θ = C1 exp(−ζ1² Fo) J0(ζ r/r0).

definitions.name: _one_term_sphere
definitions.documentation:
First-term (Fo > 0.2) transient solution for a sphere of radius r0 in convection.

Eigenvalue ζ1 solves 1 − ζ cot ζ = Bi on (0, π); C1 = 4 (sin ζ − ζ cos ζ)/(2ζ − sin 2ζ). Centre and
surface temperatures follow θ = C1 exp(−ζ1² Fo) (sin(ζ r/r0)/(ζ r/r0)).

definitions.name: _finite_difference_2d
definitions.documentation:
Steady 2-D conduction (Laplace) nodal temperatures by Gauss-Seidel on a square grid.

Dirichlet temperatures on all four edges; the interior is iterated until the largest change is below
1e-9 K. Grid is [nodes_x, nodes_y] with 3..50 nodes per side (interior nodes are the unknowns).

definitions.name: _band_fraction
definitions.documentation: Blackbody band fraction F(λ1→λ2) = ∫E_bλ dλ / (σ T⁴) by numeric integration of Planck's law.

definitions.name: _plane_wall_series
definitions.documentation:
Composite plane wall: conduction + contact + convection resistances in series (per unit area).

layers = [[L, k, R_c], ...] from the hot side; R_c is the contact resistance AFTER that layer.
Temperatures are reported from the hot surface through each interface to the cold surface.

definitions.name: _effectiveness_counter
definitions.documentation:
Counter-flow effectiveness ε = (1 − e^(−NTU(1−Cr)))/(1 − Cr e^(−NTU(1−Cr))), with the Cr = 1 limit
ε = NTU/(1 + NTU).

A procedure (rather than an equation) so the inverse of Cr is found by 1-D root finding: the closed
form for Cr involves the W_−1 branch of the Lambert W function, which the symbolic solver resolves to
the wrong (W_0) branch.

definitions.name: _lmtd
definitions.documentation: Log-mean temperature difference via common.lmtd (the shared adapter).

definitions.name: _critical_insulation
definitions.documentation: Critical insulation radius: r_cr = k/h for a cylinder, 2k/h for a sphere.

definitions.name: _lumped_capacitance
definitions.documentation:
Lumped-capacitance transient temperature, time constant and Biot number.

Bi = h L_c / k with L_c = V/A_s; the model is valid for Bi < 0.1, so a larger Biot number is reported
as a warning rather than silently returning a suspect temperature.

definitions.name: _dittus_boelter
definitions.documentation:
Dittus–Boelter turbulent internal-flow correlation.

Nu = 0.023 Re^0.8 Pr^n with n = 0.4 (heating) or 0.3 (cooling); h = Nu k/D. Validity Re > 10000 and
0.6 < Pr < 160 is checked and reported as warnings (not enforced) so off-range use is visible.

definitions.name: _laminar_nu
definitions.documentation: Fully developed laminar internal-flow Nusselt number (constant, independent of Re).

imports: from engineering_sim.science.mech.core import Calc, MechError, V, section
from scipy import integrate, optimize, special
coverage: Packaged implementation; no direct test reference found.

definitions.name: _humid_air_state
definitions.documentation: Moist-air state from dry-bulb T, relative humidity and total pressure (HAPropsSI).

definitions.name: _psych_chart
definitions.documentation: Psychrometric chart spec: T vs W with constant-RH lines at the calculator's total pressure.

definitions.name: _moist_air_mixing
definitions.documentation: Adiabatic mixing of two moist-air streams by humidity-ratio and enthalpy balance.

definitions.name: _sensible_process
definitions.documentation: Sensible heating/cooling at constant humidity ratio: Q = m_da (H2 − H1).

definitions.name: _adiabatic_humidification
definitions.documentation:
Adiabatic (evaporative) humidification: constant enthalpy, water sprayed in.

Outlet humidity ratio W2 = W1 + m_w/m_da at H2 = H1; the outlet temperature follows the wet-bulb
(constant-enthalpy) line toward saturation.

definitions.name: _cooling_dehumidification
definitions.documentation:
Cooling and dehumidification: air leaves saturated at T2 (below the inlet dew point).

Condensate m_cond = m_da (W1 − W2) leaves at T2; coil load
Q = m_da (H1 − H2) − m_cond c_pw (T2 − 273.15 K).

definitions.name: _apparatus_dew_point
definitions.documentation:
Apparatus dew point (ADP) of a cooling coil from the room condition and sensible heat ratio.

The room condition line through (T_room, W_room) has slope dW/dT = c_p (1 − SHR)/(SHR h_fg). The ADP
is where this line meets the saturation curve (RH = 1), found by scanning down from the room dew point.

imports: from engineering_sim.science.mech.core import Calc, MechError, V, section
coverage: Packaged implementation; no direct test reference found.

definitions.name: _cylinder_speed
definitions.documentation: Extension and retraction speeds of a double-acting cylinder from the flow rate and geometry.

definitions.name: _accumulator
definitions.documentation: Gas-charged accumulator sizing with the polytropic gas law P·V^n = const (pressures ABSOLUTE).

imports: from engineering_sim.science.mech.core import Calc, MechError, V, section
coverage: Packaged implementation; no direct test reference found.

definitions.name: _n_rev
definitions.documentation: Revolutions per power stroke from the text choice: 1 (two-stroke) or 2 (four-stroke).

definitions.name: _indicated_power
definitions.documentation: Indicated power IP = MEP · V_d · N / n_rev (V_d = total engine displacement).

definitions.name: _brake_mep
definitions.documentation: Brake mean effective pressure BMEP = 2π n_rev T / V_d (V_d = total engine displacement).

definitions.name: _volumetric_efficiency
definitions.documentation: Volumetric efficiency η_v = ṁ_a / (ρ_a V_d N / n_rev) (V_d = total engine displacement).

imports: from engineering_sim.science.mech.core import Calc, MechError, V, section
coverage: Packaged implementation; no direct test reference found.

definitions.name: _thermocouple_poly
definitions.documentation:
Thermocouple emf from a user-supplied polynomial in the junction−reference temperature difference.

V = Σ c_i (T_junction − T_ref)^i, with coefficients c_i in V/K^i (c0 in V, c1 in V/K, …). The
coefficients are user inputs from a calibration or a published table (e.g. NIST ITS-90); none are built
in because the standard coefficients are temperature-range specific and must not be recalled.

definitions.name: _rtd_cvd
definitions.documentation:
Platinum RTD resistance by the Callendar–Van Dusen equation.

T is an absolute temperature (K); it is converted internally to T_C = T − 273.15 (°C). Then
R = R0 (1 + A·T_C + B·T_C² + C·(T_C − 100)·T_C³) for T_C < 0 °C and R = R0 (1 + A·T_C + B·T_C²) for
T_C ≥ 0 °C. A, B, C are user inputs; IEC 60751 nominals (A = 3.9083e-3, B = −5.775e-7,
C = −4.183e-12) are commonly quoted but not built in.

definitions.name: _alias
definitions.documentation:
Aliased frequency when a signal at f_sig is sampled at f_s (fold-back / undersampling).

f_alias = |f_sig − f_s · round(f_sig/f_s)|: the distance from f_sig to the nearest multiple of the
sample rate. For f_sig ≤ f_s/2 (satisfying Nyquist) this returns f_sig unchanged.

definitions.name: _uncertainty
definitions.documentation:
Combined standard uncertainty of a function of measured variables by first-order propagation.

setup = {"expr": "a*b + c**2", "variables": {"a": [value, uncertainty], …}}. Partial derivatives are
taken with sympy; for uncorrelated inputs u_y = sqrt(Σ (∂f/∂x_i · u_i)²). All values are plain numbers
(consistent units, stated by the user); sensitivities are returned in the same output/input units.

imports: from engineering_sim.science.mech.core import Calc, MechError, V, section, safe_expr
coverage: Packaged implementation; no direct test reference found.

imports: from engineering_sim.science.mech.core import Calc, V, section
coverage: Packaged implementation; no direct test reference found.

definitions.name: _mass_inertia
definitions.documentation:
Mass moment of inertia of a standard solid about a centroidal axis, plus parallel-axis shift.

``solid`` is a dict: {'shape': 'rod'|'disk'|'cylinder'|'sphere'|'shell'|'block', 'm': mass kg,
and the needed dimension(s)}: rod → 'L' (length); disk/cylinder (central axis) / sphere / shell (thin SPHERICAL shell, about a diameter) → 'r'; block → 'a','b'. Solid-cylinder transverse axis m(3r²+h²)/12 is not included
(the two in-plane side lengths). ``d`` is the parallel-axis offset from that centroidal axis.
Returns I_c (about the centroidal axis) and I = I_c + m·d².

imports: from engineering_sim.science.mech.core import Calc, MechError, V, section
coverage: Test-text reference only; not measured branch/function coverage.

definitions.name: _springback
definitions.documentation:
Sheet-bending springback from the constant neutral-axis length.

R_i/R_f = 1 − 3x + 4x³ with x = σ_y R_i/(E t) (elastic-perfectly-plastic radius recovery); the neutral
axis at mid-thickness keeps its length, θ_i(R_i + t/2) = θ_f(R_f + t/2), so θ_f/θ_i = (R_i + t/2)/(R_f + t/2).

definitions.name: _injection_cooling_time
_weld_cooling_rate
definitions.documentation: Weld cooling rate (3-D thick-plate Rosenthal): R = 2πk(T_c − T_0)²/H.

definitions.name: _am_layer_count
definitions.documentation: 3-D printing layer count, rounded UP to a whole number of layers.

imports: from engineering_sim.science.mech.core import Calc, MechError, V, section
coverage: Packaged implementation; no direct test reference found.

definitions.name: _principal_3d
definitions.documentation: Eigenvalues of the symmetric Cauchy stress tensor, sorted σ1 ≥ σ2 ≥ σ3.

definitions.name: _failure
definitions.documentation:
Factors of safety from the principal stresses of a plane-stress state (third principal = 0).

Ductile: von Mises (distortion energy) and Tresca (maximum shear) against S_y.
Brittle / unequal strength: Rankine (maximum normal), Coulomb–Mohr and modified Mohr against S_ut, S_uc.
σA, σB are the two in-plane principal stresses with σA ≥ σB.

definitions.name: _composite_beam
definitions.documentation:
Transformed-section bending of a stacked rectangular composite beam.

layers: bottom-to-top [[b (m), h (m), E (Pa)], ...]; M bending moment (N·m, sagging positive, puts the
top in compression). Each layer is transformed to the reference modulus E_ref by width n·b with
n = E/E_ref; stress in a layer at height y from the neutral axis is σ = −n M y / I_t.

imports: from engineering_sim.science.mech.core import Calc, MechError, V, section
coverage: Packaged implementation; no direct test reference found.

definitions.name: _miller
definitions.documentation:
Miller indices (hkl) from intercepts with the unit-cell axes.

intercepts: [x, y, z] as fractions of the lattice parameters; 0 means the plane is parallel to that
axis (intercept at infinity). The indices are the smallest integers proportional to the reciprocal
intercepts.

definitions.name: _hall_petch
definitions.documentation: Hall-Petch yield strength via common.hall_petch (single shared implementation).

definitions.name: _fick_second
definitions.documentation: Non-steady diffusion into a semi-infinite solid: C(x,t) = Cs - (Cs - C0) erf(x/(2 sqrt(D t))).

definitions.name: _creep
definitions.documentation: Steady-state (secondary) creep rate by the Norton power law: edot = A sigma^n exp(-Q/RT).

definitions.name: _crystal_density
definitions.documentation: Theoretical density: rho = n A_molar / (N_A a^3).

definitions.name: _diffusion
definitions.documentation: Arrhenius diffusion coefficient: D = D0 exp(-Q/(R T)).

definitions.name: _hardness_uts
definitions.documentation: Approximate ultimate tensile strength from Brinell hardness: UTS(MPa) ≈ 3.45 HB (steels).

definitions.name: _elastic_bounds
definitions.documentation:
Isotropic two-phase elastic bounds via common.elastic_bounds (single shared implementation).

The E values are the isotropic Young's modulus E = 9KG/(3K+G) corresponding to each K, G bound.

definitions.name: _laminate
definitions.documentation:
Classical lamination theory: A, B, D matrices and in-plane constants from a ply list.

plies: [[thickness (m), angle (deg)], ...] bottom-to-top, one material for all plies. Reduced
stiffness Q from E1, E2, nu12, G12; transformed to global axes by the standard CLT transformation;
A = sum Q_bar t, B = 1/2 sum Q_bar (z^2 - z0^2), D = 1/3 sum Q_bar (z^3 - z0^3). In-plane (membrane)
constants come from the compliance a = A^-1: E_x = 1/(h a11), E_y = 1/(h a22), G_xy = 1/(h a66),
nu_xy = -a12/a11. These are exact for symmetric laminates (B = 0); for unsymmetric layups they come
from A alone and ignore bending-extension coupling.

imports: from engineering_sim.science.mech.core import Calc, MechError, V, section

definitions.name: _expr_text
definitions.documentation: Pull the expression string out of its one-element JSON-list wrapper.

definitions.name: _parse
definitions.documentation: Parse ``expr`` with core.safe_expr; only ``var`` (and ``extra_syms``) may appear free.

definitions.name: _lambdified
definitions.documentation: numpy lambdify of ``parsed`` over ``order`` (a tuple of symbols), or raise a user-facing error.

definitions.name: _sym_op
definitions.documentation:
Run a symbolic operation (diff/integrate/transform) under core.time_limit.

A timeout (``_Timeout``) or a sympy failure becomes a user-facing MechError, so a hard-to-handle
expression fails fast instead of hanging the worker thread.

definitions.name: _real_value
definitions.documentation: Real float from a sympy/numpy numeric result; MechError if non-numeric or meaningfully complex.

definitions.name: _derivative
definitions.documentation: Symbolic and numeric derivative of f(x): derivative_expr (string) and its value at x = at.

definitions.name: _integral
definitions.documentation: Indefinite integral (string) and the definite integral of f(x) over [a, b].

definitions.name: _laplace
definitions.documentation: Laplace transform L{f(t)}(s) (string) and its value at s = s_val.

definitions.name: _fourier
definitions.documentation: Fourier transform F{f(x)}(k) (sympy convention F(k)=∫f(x)e^(-2πikx)dx); value at k = k_val.

definitions.name: _newton
definitions.documentation: Newton–Raphson root of f(x)=0 from a starting guess x0 (iterated to 1e-12 relative tolerance).

definitions.name: _simpson
definitions.documentation: Composite Simpson's rule for ∫_a^b f(x) dx with n equal panels (n even). Exact for cubics.

definitions.name: _runge_kutta
definitions.documentation: Classic 4th-order Runge–Kutta for y' = f(x, y) over n steps of size h from (x0, y0).

definitions.name: _stats
definitions.documentation: Mean, sample/population variance and standard deviation of a data list (sample std uses n-1).

definitions.name: _regression
definitions.documentation: Ordinary least-squares fit y = slope*x + intercept with Pearson r and r².

definitions.name: _confidence
definitions.documentation: Two-sided confidence interval for the mean of a data list using a Student-t quantile.

definitions.name: _unit_convert
definitions.documentation: Convert a value between any two pint units via the shared core registry (offset units supported).

definitions.name: _vector_ops
definitions.documentation: 3-D vector algebra: magnitudes, dot and cross products, resultant and included angle.

definitions.name: _matrix_ops
definitions.documentation: Determinant, trace and inverse of a square 2x2 or 3x3 matrix.

definitions.name: _eigen
definitions.documentation: Eigenvalues (descending) and unit eigenvectors of a real symmetric 2x2 or 3x3 matrix.

definitions.name: _triangle_centroid
definitions.documentation: Centroid (average of vertices) of a triangle given by three [x, y] vertices.

imports: from engineering_sim.science.mech.core import Calc, MechError, Q_, V, _Timeout, safe_expr, section, time_limit
coverage: Test-text reference only; not measured branch/function coverage.

definitions.name: _theta3
definitions.signature: a, b, c, d, th2, br=1.0

definitions.name: _grashof
definitions.documentation: Grashof classification of a four-bar from its four link lengths (json [a, b, c, d]).

definitions.name: _fourbar_position
definitions.documentation: Four-bar vector-loop closure: coupler/rocker angles, transmission angle and diagonal at theta2.

definitions.name: _fourbar_toggle
definitions.documentation:
Toggle (dead-centre) crank angles of a crank-rocker and the rocker's extreme angles.

The rocker reverses when the crank and coupler are collinear (sin(theta2 - theta3) = 0); the two
toggle crank angles are found by scanning a full crank revolution and refining each sign change.
The rocker extreme angles theta4_1/theta4_2 are reported for the crossed branch (theta4 = phi + beta).
Both assembly branches reach their rocker extremes at the SAME toggle crank angles; for the open branch
(theta4 = phi - beta) the extremes are the mirror values 2*pi - theta4 in this ground-frame convention.

definitions.name: _fourbar_accel
definitions.documentation:
Four-bar coupler and rocker angular accelerations alpha3, alpha4 (vector-loop acceleration).

Differentiating the four-bar velocity loop once more and separating real/imaginary parts gives the
linear system
    b cos(theta3) alpha3 - c cos(theta4) alpha4 = A
    b sin(theta3) alpha3 - c sin(theta4) alpha4 = B
with
    A = -a alpha2 cos(theta2) + a omega2^2 sin(theta2) + b omega3^2 sin(theta3) - c omega4^2 sin(theta4)
    B = -a alpha2 sin(theta2) - a omega2^2 cos(theta2) - b omega3^2 cos(theta3) + c omega4^2 cos(theta4)
solved for
    alpha3 = (B cos(theta4) - A sin(theta4))/(b sin(theta3 - theta4))
    alpha4 = (B cos(theta3) - A sin(theta3))/(c sin(theta3 - theta4)).

definitions.name: _slider_crank
definitions.documentation:
In-line/offset slider-crank position, velocity and acceleration (constant crank speed).

geometry = [r, L, e]: crank radius r, connecting-rod length L, offset e (crank pivot to slider
axis; 0 for in-line). g = r sin(theta2) - e; h = L cos(phi) = +/-sqrt(L^2 - g^2), signed by the
branch (open: h > 0, crossed: h < 0); phi = atan2(g, h) so phi agrees with its omega_phi/alpha_phi.

definitions.name: _cam_profile
definitions.documentation:
Follower displacement/velocity/acceleration/jerk for a standard rise motion law.

law: 'uniform' (constant velocity), 'shm' (simple harmonic), 'cycloidal' or 'poly345' (3-4-5
polynomial). All laws act on the rise interval theta in [0, beta]; dwells are outside (not modelled).

definitions.name: _gear_train_value
definitions.documentation: Signed train value of a simple or compound gear train (Willis-free; planetary uses its own calc).

definitions.name: _balance_one_plane
definitions.documentation: Resultant unbalance (m*r and angle) of rotating masses in one plane.

definitions.name: _balance_two_plane
definitions.documentation:
Two-plane (dynamic) balancing correction masses.

masses = [[m (kg), r (m), theta (deg), z (m)], ...] with z the axial position; planes = [z_A, z_B].
Solves force balance (sum u + u_A + u_B = 0) and moment balance (sum z*u + z_A*u_A + z_B*u_B = 0)
in complex form for the correction m*r products u_A, u_B.

definitions.name: _slider_crank_dynamic
definitions.documentation:
Dynamic (inertia + gas) crank torque and pin/bearing forces of a slider-crank.

geometry = [r, L, e] (m); omega (rad/s, signed); F_gas (N) is the gas force on the piston, positive
pushing the piston TOWARD the crank (so the quasi-static limit matches ``crank_effort``); m_piston,
m_rod (kg) with its CG at l_cg (m) from the crank pin, and m_crankpin (kg) the rotating mass lumped
at the crank radius. The rod is replaced by two lumped end masses that preserve its total mass and CG
(piston side m_rod l_cg/L reciprocates, crank side m_rod(1 - l_cg/L) rotates). Piston net force in +x
is F_gas + m_recip*a toward the crank (a positive in +x, away from the crank) with the exact slider
acceleration a, and the crank torque follows from the power
balance T*omega = (net piston force)*(piston velocity), i.e. T = F_rod r (g cos(theta2) + h sin(theta2))/L.

definitions.name: _slider_dynamic_chart
definitions.documentation: Crank torque and pin/bearing forces vs crank angle over one revolution (example defaults).

imports: from engineering_sim.science.mech.core import Calc, MechError, V, section
coverage: Test-text reference only; not measured branch/function coverage.

definitions.name: _d2_d3
definitions.documentation:
d2 = E[range] and d3 = std[range] of n iid standard normals, by numeric integration.

P(range ≤ x) = n ∫ [Φ(u) − Φ(u − x)]^{n−1} φ(u) du; then d2 = ∫(1 − F_R) dx and
E[R²] = ∫ 2x(1 − F_R) dx, both evaluated with fixed Gauss–Legendre quadrature (80 nodes over
u ∈ [−10, 10] and x ∈ [0, 10]). Reproduces the published d2 table (d2(2) = 2/√π, d2(5) = 2.3259).

definitions.name: _d2_star
definitions.documentation: d2* = √(d2² + d3²): the range correction for a SINGLE range (g = 1), used by K2/K3 in gauge R&R.

definitions.name: _measurement_stats
definitions.documentation: Summary statistics of repeated measurements (repeatability basis).

definitions.name: _acceptance
definitions.documentation: Probability of acceptance for a single sampling plan, hypergeometric (finite lot).

definitions.name: _oc_binomial
definitions.documentation: Probability of acceptance, binomial (infinite lot / with replacement).

definitions.name: _gauge_blocks
definitions.documentation:
Gauge-block combination by minimum-block-count dynamic programming.

Sizes are scaled to 0.5 µm so 0.0005 mm blocks are representable exactly. The 0/1 knapsack DP stores
the fewest blocks that reach each length, so among several exact stacks the one using the fewest
blocks is returned (e.g. target 5 mm from {1..5} mm → {5}, not {3+2}).

imports: from engineering_sim.science.mech.core import Calc, MechError, V, section
coverage: Packaged implementation; no direct test reference found.

definitions.name: check_case
definitions.documentation: Return (ok, detail) for one oracle case.

definitions.name: _abs_tol
definitions.documentation:
Relative comparison only, unless the expected value is exactly zero.

 A fixed SI abs_tol (formerly 1e-9) silently accepted any result for small SI quantities — wear
 coefficients, film thicknesses, compressibility — so an Archard oracle expecting 9e-10 passed at 2e-11
. A case may still set "abs_tol" explicitly (e.g. round-off at a free surface).

definitions.name: verify
definitions.documentation: Run every oracle (optionally one section); report per case plus coverage of calculators.

coverage: Test-text reference only; not measured branch/function coverage.

imports: from engineering_sim.science.mech.core import Calc, V, section
coverage: Packaged implementation; no direct test reference found.

definitions.name: _cylindrical_shell
definitions.documentation:
ASME UG-27 cylinder: circumferential-stress (longitudinal joint) and longitudinal-stress
(circumferential joint) thickness and MAWP; the required thickness is the larger, the MAWP the smaller.

definitions.name: _spherical_shell
definitions.documentation: ASME UG-27 sphere: required thickness and MAWP with thin-shell validity checks.

definitions.name: _head_hemispherical
definitions.documentation: ASME UG-32 hemispherical head thickness (same membrane form as a sphere) with validity checks.

definitions.name: _nozzle_reinforcement
definitions.documentation:
Simplified UG-37 area-replacement for a radial nozzle (correction factor F = 1).

A_req = d·t_r + 2·t_n·t_r·(1 − f_r1) is the area removed from the shell wall (the second term is the
shell metal displaced by the nozzle wall, credited only in proportion f_r1 = S_n/S). Available
reinforcement is the shell excess A1 = d·(t − t_r) − 2·t_n·(t − t_r)·(1 − f_r1) over the opening, the
nozzle-wall excess A2 = 2·h_n·(t_n − t_rn)·f_r2 on both sides of the wall, and the weld area A_weld.
Negative A1/A2 (too-thin shell/nozzle) contribute 0 to A_avail, with a warning.

definitions.name: _pipe_support_spacing
definitions.documentation:
Maximum pipe support spacing from bending-stress and mid-span deflection limits.

The span condition is a user choice: simply supported (M = w·L²/8, δ = 5·w·L⁴/(384·E·I)) or
continuous (M = w·L²/10, δ = w·L⁴/(185·E·I)) — both recalled beam constants. The bending-stress
limit σ = M/Z gives L_stress; the deflection limit gives L_defl; the allowable spacing is the smaller.

imports: from engineering_sim.science.mech.core import Calc, MechError, V, section
coverage: Packaged implementation; no direct test reference found.

definitions.name: _weibull_fit
definitions.documentation:
Weibull β, η from a complete (uncensored) failure-time sample, two ways:

- Median-rank regression (Bernard median ranks F_i = (i − 0.3)/(n + 0.4)) on the linearised CDF
  ln(ln(1/(1−F))) = β ln t − β ln η: ordinary least squares, slope = β, η = exp(−intercept/β).
- Maximum likelihood via scipy.stats.weibull_min.fit with location fixed at 0 (2-parameter Weibull).

definitions.name: _weibull_hazard
definitions.documentation: Weibull hazard rate and pdf at time t: h(t) = (β/η)(t/η)^(β−1), f(t) = h(t)·R(t).

definitions.name: _weibull_mttf
definitions.documentation: Weibull mean time to failure: MTTF = η·Γ(1 + 1/β).

definitions.name: _series
definitions.documentation: Reliability of n independent components in series (system survives only if every component does).

definitions.name: _parallel
definitions.documentation: Reliability of n independent components in parallel (system fails only if every component fails).

definitions.name: _reliability_index
definitions.documentation:
Reliability index β and probability of failure for normally distributed load and strength.

Strength S ~ N(μ_S, σ_S) and load L ~ N(μ_L, σ_L) are independent, so the margin M = S − L is
N(μ_S − μ_L, sqrt(σ_S² + σ_L²)). β = (μ_S − μ_L)/sqrt(σ_S² + σ_L²); p_f = P(M < 0) = Φ(−β).

imports: from engineering_sim.science.mech.core import Calc, MechError, V, section
coverage: Packaged implementation; no direct test reference found.

definitions.name: _tilted_irradiance
definitions.documentation:
Total irradiance on a tilted plane: isotropic-sky Liu–Jordan model.

G_T = G_bn·cos θ (beam on the tilted plane) + G_d·(1+cos β)/2 (sky-diffuse view factor)
    + (G_bn·cos θ_z + G_d)·ρ_g·(1−cos β)/2 (ground-reflected, isotropic).

definitions.name: _steam_enthalpy
definitions.documentation:
Enthalpy of the generated steam.

'saturated': saturated vapour at P_steam (CoolProp state with quality Q = 1), so a temperature just
below T_sat can never silently resolve to liquid water. 'superheated': the T_steam/P_steam state,
rejected with a clear error when that state is a liquid (T_steam below T_sat).

definitions.name: _solar_collector
definitions.documentation:
Hottel–Whillier–Bliss flat-plate collector: useful heat and instantaneous efficiency.

Q_u and η are both signed — a collector running at night or at high ΔT loses heat (negative Q_u, η).
Zero irradiance is rejected (efficiency is undefined, and the heat gain is a pure loss there).

definitions.name: _boiler_efficiency
definitions.documentation: Direct-method boiler efficiency: η = ṁ_s(h_steam − h_feed) / (ṁ_f·HHV).

definitions.name: _steam_generation
definitions.documentation: Steam generation rate from a heat input: ṁ_s = Q_in / (h_steam − h_feed).

definitions.name: _geothermal_efficiency
definitions.documentation: Geothermal thermal and utilization efficiency, with clear errors on non-physical inputs.

imports: from engineering_sim.science.mech.core import Calc, MechError, V, section
coverage: Packaged implementation; no direct test reference found.

definitions.name: _mm
definitions.documentation: 4x4 matrix product.

definitions.name: _fk_planar
definitions.documentation: Tip position [x, y] of a planar n-link arm (links and angles in SI/rad).

definitions.name: _jacobian_planar
definitions.documentation: 2xn geometric (basic) Jacobian of a planar n-link arm: J = [dx/dth; dy/dth].

definitions.name: _poly
definitions.documentation: Evaluate a polynomial and its first two derivatives at t -> (q, qd, qdd).

definitions.name: _serial_dof
definitions.documentation: DoF of a serial open chain from its joint types: R/P=1, U/C=2, S=3 degrees of freedom each.

definitions.name: _dh_forward
definitions.documentation: Denavit–Hartenberg forward kinematics. Rows [a (m), alpha (deg), d (m), theta (deg)].

definitions.name: _homogeneous_transform
definitions.documentation: Build a 4x4 homogeneous transform from a rotation matrix and translation, and its inverse.

definitions.name: _planar_2r_ik
definitions.documentation:
Closed-form inverse kinematics of a planar 2R arm: two elbow branches.

θ2 is the joint-2 angle relative to link 1. The branch with θ2 = +acos(c2) is elbow-DOWN in the
standard (Spong) sense (elbow below the base–tip line); θ2 = −acos(c2) is elbow-UP. `theta1`/
`theta2` carry the elbow-down branch, `theta1_b`/`theta2_b` the elbow-up branch.

definitions.name: _planar_3r_ik
definitions.documentation: Closed-form IK of a planar 3R arm for a given tip position AND orientation (phi = theta1+theta2+theta3).

definitions.name: _numeric_ik
definitions.documentation: Numeric IK of a general planar n-link arm by damped least squares (deterministic).

definitions.name: _planar_jacobian
definitions.documentation:
Geometric Jacobian of a planar n-link arm and joint velocities for a given tip velocity.

joint_vel is the minimum-norm (pseudo-inverse) solution of J θ̇ = v; `residual` reports how much of
the requested tip velocity is actually achieved (‖J θ̇ − v‖), which is non-zero only at a singularity.

definitions.name: _planar_2r_dynamics
definitions.documentation:
Closed-form Lagrange/Newton–Euler torques of a planar 2R arm (relative joint angles, gravity −y).

θ1 is the joint-1 angle from +x; θ2 is the joint-2 angle RELATIVE to link 1 (not absolute), so the
inertia-matrix coupling term carries cos θ2. Gravity acts along −y.

definitions.name: _payload_capacity
definitions.documentation:
Static payload capacity of a planar 2R arm (links as point masses at mid-length, gravity −y).

The payload sits at the tip. Each joint limits the payload through |τ_link + m·g·arm| ≤ τ_max, solved exactly
for either sign of the link torque and moment arm (feasible interval clipped at m ≥ 0; capacity = upper end). A joint whose payload arm is ≈ 0
(payload directly above/below it) imposes no static limit and is skipped with a warning.

imports: from engineering_sim.science.mech.core import Calc, MechError, V, section
coverage: Packaged implementation; no direct test reference found.

definitions.name: _geom_outputs
definitions.documentation: Common output keys for a section (excludes the torsion constant J_t).

definitions.name: _rect_geom
definitions.documentation:
Full geometry of a composite of axis-aligned rectangles.

Each row is [b, h, xc, yc]: width b, height h, centroid at (xc, yc). Rectangles must not overlap.
Returns area, centroid, centroidal second moments Ix/Iy/Ixy, polar J, elastic section moduli
Sx/Sy (= I/c to the extreme fibre), plastic moduli Zx/Zy (equal-area axis by bisection), radii of
gyration rx/ry, shape factors, and principal moments/angle.

definitions.name: _plastic_rects
definitions.documentation:
Plastic modulus about a horizontal ('x') or vertical ('y') axis by bisecting the equal-area axis.

The equal-area axis is found by bisection on the coordinate perpendicular to ``axis``; the plastic
modulus is then Z = Q_above + Q_below = 2·Q_above − A·(bar − c), where Q_above is the first moment of
the material on the positive side of the axis about that axis and ``bar`` the centroid coordinate.

definitions.name: _poly_geom
definitions.documentation:
Full geometry of a simple polygon given as [[x, y], ...] vertices (m), in any winding order.

Area, centroid and second moments use Green's-theorem edge sums (exact for any simple polygon); the
plastic modulus Zx is obtained by bisecting the equal-area horizontal axis with an edge-integral
half-plane clip (exact, and correct for concave polygons). Concave sections are also served by the
rectangle-composite procedure.

definitions.name: _q_edge
definitions.documentation: ∫ p(t)·t dt along a straight segment from (pa, ta) to (pb, tb); t is the distance coordinate.

definitions.name: _poly_half
definitions.documentation:
(area, first-moment-about-the-line) of the part of a CCW polygon on the positive side of the line
y = c (axis == 1) or x = c (axis == 0). Exact for any simple polygon.

The loop below is the horizontal-axis form: it integrates ∮ x dy (area) and ∮ x(y−c) dy (first moment)
along the polygon edges on the y > c side, where the clip line y = c contributes nothing because dy = 0
there. For a vertical axis the analogous edge sum would be ∮ y dx, which (a) is the negative of the
area for a CCW polygon and (b) also omits the non-zero contribution of the vertical clip line, so it
breaks for concave polygons. We therefore swap x↔y and reverse the vertex order (a reflection across
y = x, which preserves CCW orientation) and reuse the horizontal-axis logic verbatim.

definitions.name: _plastic_poly
definitions.documentation: Plastic modulus of a polygon about a horizontal (axis=1) or vertical (axis=0) axis by bisection.

definitions.name: _channel_shear_center
definitions.documentation:
Shear centre of a thin-walled channel (uniform thickness t): distance e from the web centreline,
on the side opposite the flange toes, e = 3·b²/(6·b + h). b = flange width measured from the web
centreline to the flange tip; h = web depth measured between flange centrelines.

imports: from engineering_sim.science.mech.core import Calc, MechError, V, section
coverage: Packaged implementation; no direct test reference found.

definitions.name: _beam_solution
definitions.documentation:
Static deflection/slope of a stepped round shaft by exact numerical integration of M/(EI).

case      'simply_supported' (two supports at a, b) or 'cantilever' (fixed at x = 0)
segments  [[length, diameter], ...] in m, in order from x = 0
loads     [[x, F], ...] point loads, F positive downward
supports  [a, b] for simply supported (positions in m); pass [] for a cantilever (not used)
E         Young's modulus (Pa)

The integration grid carries a node at every segment boundary, load position and support, so the
trapezoid rule on M/EI (piecewise linear with those nodes) is exact — no step-size error from an
EI jump or an off-node load. Returns {'x','y','slope','reactions','L'}: y and slope of the
upward-positive y axis on a fine uniform grid (the kink nodes included), reactions [[x, R], ...]
(upward positive), and total length. Sagging-positive moment gives downward (negative) y.

definitions.name: _eval_points
definitions.documentation: Sorted x positions at which deflection/slope are reported (loads + supports).

definitions.name: _shaft_deflection
definitions.documentation: Deflection and slope at loads/supports plus maxima, for a stepped shaft.

definitions.name: _shaft_critical_speed
definitions.documentation:
First bending critical speed of a stepped shaft by Rayleigh's method (static deflections under
the mass weights). ω = sqrt(g·Σ m_i·δ_i / Σ m_i·δ_i²) with δ_i the deflections at the masses.

imports: from engineering_sim.science.mech.core import Calc, MechError, V, section
coverage: Packaged implementation; no direct test reference found.

definitions.name: _spring_geometry
definitions.documentation: Total coils, solid length and free length from active coils and the end condition.

definitions.name: _spring_buckling
definitions.documentation:
Compression-spring buckling: critical deflection, absolute-stability length, stable flag.

Shigley form δ_cr = C₁′·L0·[1 − √(1 − C₂′/λ_eff²)] with C₁′ = E/(2(E − G)),
C₂′ = 2π²(E − G)/(2G + E) and λ_eff = α·L0/D. Buckling is possible only when
L0 ≥ L0_crit = (πD/α)·√(2(E − G)/(2G + E)); for L0 < L0_crit the spring is absolutely
stable and δ_cr has no real value (reported null, stable = 1).

definitions.name: _belleville_load
definitions.signature: E, nu, Do, K, t, h, delta
definitions.documentation: Almen–László load for a coned-disc (Belleville) spring at deflection delta.

definitions.name: _belleville_k1
definitions.documentation: DIN 2092 geometry constant K1 = (1/π)·((C−1)/C)²/((C+1)/(C−1) − 2/ln C).

definitions.name: _belleville_m
definitions.documentation: Original Almen–László geometry constant M = (6/(π·ln C))·((C−1)/C)² (C = D_o/D_i).

definitions.name: _belleville
definitions.documentation:
Belleville (disc) spring load–deflection (Almen–László theory).

C = D_o/D_i; F = 4E·δ/((1−ν²)·K·D_o²)·[(h−δ)(h−δ/2)·t + t³] with K = K1 (DIN 2092) or
M (original Almen–László) as selected by ``form``. Valid for 0 ≤ δ ≤ h (flat at δ = h).

definitions.name: _spring_fatigue
definitions.documentation:
Spring-wire fatigue: wire strength, torsional endurance and Goodman/Gerber safety factors.

S_ut = A/d^m with d in mm and A in MPa·mm^m (wire-strength table, Shigley Table 10-4 form); in
coherent SI this is S_ut = A·(1 mm/d)^m with A = S_ut at d = 1 mm (Pa). S_su = 0.67·S_ut.
Zimmerli-type test data (S_sa, S_sm measured at a nonzero mean stress) convert to the fully
reversed endurance with the SAME criterion that is then applied: Goodman S_se = S_sa/(1 − S_sm/S_su) and
Gerber S_se,G = S_sa/(1 − (S_sm/S_su)²). Goodman and Gerber safety factors then follow for the working
alternating/mean shear (τ_a, τ_m).

imports: from engineering_sim.science.mech.core import Calc, MechError, V, section
coverage: Packaged implementation; no direct test reference found.

definitions.name: _resultant
definitions.documentation: Resultant of coplanar forces [[F (N), angle (deg from +x), x (m), y (m)], ...] about the origin.

definitions.name: _truss
definitions.documentation:
Pin-jointed plane truss by the method of joints (all joints at once as a linear system).

nodes    [[x_m, y_m], ...]
members  [[i, j], ...]            node indices (0-based)
supports [[node, 'x'|'y'], ...]   one reaction component per entry (pin = x and y, roller = one)
loads    [[node, Fx_N, Fy_N], ...]
Statically determinate only: members + reactions must equal 2 x nodes and the matrix full rank.
The method of sections gives identical forces for a determinate truss, so one solver serves both.

definitions.name: _rigid_body
definitions.documentation:
Three unknown reaction components on one planar rigid body (frame/machine member).

loads     [[Fx_N, Fy_N, x_m, y_m], ...] and optional couples [[M_Nm], ...] in 'couples'
unknowns  exactly 3 rows [[angle_deg, x_m, y_m], ...]: line of action direction and point
Solves sum Fx = 0, sum Fy = 0, sum M_origin = 0 for the three magnitudes (negative = opposite sense).

definitions.name: _composite
definitions.documentation:
Composite centroid / centre of gravity: parts [[w, x, y, z], ...], w = area, volume, mass or weight
(consistent in one list; negative w for holes/cut-outs).

definitions.name: _mohr_like_force_chart
definitions.documentation: Force polygon for the resultant calculator (tip-to-tail).

definitions.name: _fluid_state_TP
definitions.documentation: Real-fluid state at (T, P): density, enthalpy, entropy, internal energy, cp, cv.

definitions.name: _fluid_state_TQ
definitions.documentation: Real-fluid two-phase state at (T, quality Q): saturated pressure and mixture properties.

definitions.name: _joule_thomson
definitions.documentation:
Joule-Thomson coefficient mu = (dT/dP)_h by central finite difference on h (CoolProp states).

mu = -(dh/dP)_T / (dh/dT)_P, with (dh/dP)_T and (dh/dT)_P evaluated by central differences on
common.fluid_state; the denominator is approximately cp. Stated as a numerical finite difference.
The four stencil states must share one single phase, otherwise a phase boundary is being straddled
and the finite difference is meaningless (raises MechError).

definitions.documentation: Saturation curve points from common.saturation, for a T-s / P-h chart.

definitions.name: _boundary_work_isothermal
definitions.documentation: Boundary work of an isothermal ideal-gas process W = P1 V1 ln(V2/V1) (procedure: numeric inversion).

definitions.name: _exergy

definitions.name: _ts_chart
definitions.documentation: T-s diagram from the saturation-dome points.

definitions.name: _ph_chart

definitions.name: _walther
definitions.documentation:
Walther (ASTM D341) viscosity–temperature relation fitted from two calibration points.

log10(log10(nu_cSt + 0.7)) = A − B·log10(T_K) is fitted through (T1, nu1) and (T2, nu2), then
evaluated at T_query. The +0.7 offset has units of cSt, so the declared m²/s values are converted to
cSt (× 1e6) inside the fit and converted back for the result.

definitions.name: _ehl_film
definitions.documentation:
Hamrock–Dowson (1977) fully-flooded elliptical-contact EHL film thickness.

Reduced modulus E' = 2 / ((1−ν1²)/E1 + (1−ν2²)/E2); dimensionless speed U = η0·u/(E'·R_x),
materials G = α·E', load W = F/(E'·R_x²) and ellipticity k ≈ 1.03·(R_y/R_x)^0.64. Minimum and
central film thickness follow the canonical power-law correlations (constants and exponents
recalled; not re-read).

otherwise the pump curve is not defined at the duty point and this raises (no flat-end clamping or
extrapolation beyond the last row).

definitions.name: _mdof
definitions.documentation:
Natural frequencies (rad/s, Hz) and mass-normalized mode shapes of an undamped MDOF system.

Solves the generalized eigenproblem K phi = omega^2 M phi with scipy.linalg.eigh; M and K are
symmetric positive-definite matrices (json, kg and N/m respectively).

definitions.name: _absorber_frequencies
definitions.documentation:
Natural frequencies of a main mass m (spring k) with a tuned/attached absorber m_a, k_a.

Roots of m m_a omega^4 - [k m_a + k_a (m + m_a)] omega^2 + k k_a = 0 (det of [K - omega^2 M]).

definitions.name: _rayleigh
definitions.documentation:
First critical speed by Rayleigh's method from measured static deflections.

masses = [[W (N), y (m)], ...]: load and its static deflection. omega_cr = sqrt(g sum(W y)/sum(W y^2)).

definitions.name: _dunkerley
definitions.documentation: First critical speed by Dunkerley's method from the individual critical speeds (rad/s).

definitions.name: _beam_frequency
definitions.documentation:
Natural frequency of a uniform beam from its (numerically found) betaL root.

bc: 'pinned-pinned', 'fixed-free' (cantilever), 'fixed-fixed' or 'free-free'. The characteristic
equation cos(betaL) cosh(betaL) = 1 (fixed-fixed/free-free) or cos(betaL) cosh(betaL) = -1
(fixed-free) is root-found per mode; pinned-pinned is closed form n pi. omega_n = beta^2 sqrt(EI/(rho A)).

definitions.name: _duhamel
definitions.documentation:
Response of an underdamped SDOF system to a force history via the Duhamel (convolution) integral.

times and forces are equal-length json lists (s and N). The force history is treated as
piecewise-constant between the given time points (a zero-order hold) and the response is built by
superposition of the exact unit-step response h(t) = (1/k)[1 - e^{-zeta wn t}(cos(wd t) +
(zeta wn/wd) sin(wd t))], i.e. x(t) = sum_j (F_j - F_{j-1}) h(t - t_j). This is exact for a
zero-order-hold force history (and for a step input) and accurate for smooth histories sampled finely.

definitions.name: _frequency_response_chart
definitions.documentation: Magnification factor and phase vs frequency ratio r (0.05..3) for the given damping ratio.

definitions.name: _weld_units
definitions.documentation:
Unit weld-group properties treating each weld as a line along its centreline.

segs: [[x1, y1, x2, y2], ...] in metres — one straight segment per weld (a polyline weld is split).
Returns A_u (m, total weld length), the centroid (x_bar, y_bar) and the second moments about the
centroidal axes I_xu, I_yu and the polar J_u = I_xu + I_yu (all in m^3 per unit throat width).

For a straight segment from (x1,y1) to (x2,y2) the integrals ∫ y'² dL and ∫ x'² dL evaluate in
closed form: ∫_0^1 (a + b t)² dt = a² + a b + b²/3, with a the offset of the start point from the
centroid and b the coordinate change along the segment.

definitions.name: _eccentric_weld
definitions.documentation:
In-plane eccentric load on a weld group: direct shear + torsional shear, vector-summed.

The load P at angle θ applied at (x_P, y_P) is reduced to a force at the centroid plus a torque
T = (x_P − x̄)Fy − (y_P − ȳ)Fx (CCW positive). Direct shear is uniform (P/A); torsional shear at a
point is τ = (T/J)(−y', x') with x', y' measured from the centroid. The resultant magnitude is
evaluated at every weld endpoint — the critical point is the one with the largest resultant.
